evidence_span: We posit that long-term project-oriented interactions is governed by four fundamental imperatives: (1) Endogenous Query Nature: Queries arise organically from task progression, rather than appearing as isolated fact-checking questions. (2) Interleaved Distribution: User inquiries are interwoven across fragmented sessions. (3) Dynamic State Evolution... (4) Proactive Contextual Alignment...

description_authors_words: we introduce Agent Market Arena (AMA), the first lifelong, real-time benchmark for evaluating LLM-based trading agents across multiple markets.
description_summary: Live, continuously running trading benchmark where LLM agents with different risk styles and memory mechanisms trade real crypto and stock markets, scored on realized financial outcomes.
external_memory_evidence: InvestorAgent ( Li et al., 2024a ) is a single-agent framework that integrates a memory module to store historical trading decisions and contextual information.
task_format_metric: cumulative/annualized return, Sharpe ratio, max drawdown on live multi-market trading
example_length: 61 days (length of the live-trading evaluation period reported in the paper (Aug 1 - Sep 30, daily decisions)) | 92 days (length of the agent-initialization/historical-grounding phase (2025-05-01 to 2025-07-31))
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] AMA is explicitly contrasted against prior trading benchmarks with a 'limited time period' (DeepFund's 24 days, yielding just 24 decisions per stock), which the paper argues offers 'little insight into how agents generalize across diverse market regimes... or longer trading horizons'; AMA instead runs as a 'lifelong, real-time' benchmark with live daily trading over months
evidence_span: DeepFund tests agent with only a limited time period of 24 days that focuses only on U.S. stocks... Such a narrow setup offers little insight into how agents generalize across diverse market regimes, particularly when transitioning between bullish and bearish conditions, or longer trading horizons.

description_authors_words: We introduce a web-scale dataset for time-continual pretraining of LLMs derived from 114 dumps of Common Crawl (CC) - orders of magnitude larger than previous continual language modeling benchmarks.
description_summary: Models are continually pretrained on successive Common Crawl snapshots and evaluated with time-stratified held-out loss and downstream accuracy, testing the tradeoff between adapting to new web data and retaining old knowledge.
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
task_format_metric: perplexity relative to Oracle + downstream zero/few-shot accuracy (Core average)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper's central framing is 'continual'/'temporal distribution shift' pretraining, not 'long-horizon'/'long-term' terminology, which does not appear to be invoked in the sections searched
evidence_span: The “Temporal” column refers to whether the continual training rounds are defined across temporal distribution shifts.

description_authors_words: this paper constructs a new benchmark named RaKE, which focuses on Relation based Knowledge Editing.
description_summary: Knowledge-editing benchmark focused on editing relations (rather than entities) in factual triplets, with metrics for whether relation-based edits succeed in LLMs.
task_format_metric: suite of relation-editing metrics across baselines
what_instead_if_absent: paper's axis is relation-centric vs. entity-centric editing scope, not duration/session count; 'long-horizon'/'long-term' terminology is not used
evidence_span: this paper constructs a new benchmark named RaKE, which focuses on Relation based Knowledge Editing

description_authors_words: We present HCAST (Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks), a benchmark of 189 machine learning engineering, cybersecurity, software engineering, and general reasoning tasks.
description_summary: Tests AI agents on 189 software/ML engineering, cybersecurity, and reasoning tasks whose difficulty is calibrated against measured human completion times, ranging from minutes to many hours.
task_format_metric: binary/continuous task success score, benchmarked against human completion-time estimates
example_length: 1 minutes (human-baseline time to complete a task (low end)) | 8 hours (human-baseline time to complete a task (high end, '8+ hours')) | 15–25 actions (mean number of agent actions (code executions) taken on successful task completions, for roughly a third of tasks)
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] HCAST operationalizes task 'time horizon' via human-expert baseline completion time, with tasks spanning from 1-2 minutes to 8+ hours; task difficulty/horizon is measured directly by how long a skilled human takes to complete it, not by an abstract notion of length.
evidence_span: HCAST tasks are designed to capture realistic challenges of widely varying complexity: they typically require multi-step sequential decision-making, are largely derived from real-world work, take between 1-2 minutes and 8+ hours, and undergo multiple stages of manual quality assurance and review.

description_authors_words: We introduce MemGUI-Bench, a comprehensive memory-centric benchmark that assesses both short-term information retention and long-term experience accumulation through pass@k protocols and staged LLM-as-judge evaluation.
description_summary: 128 mobile-GUI tasks across 26 apps organized into 64 mirror pairs (89.8% requiring cross-temporal/cross-spatial retention), testing short- vs. long-term memory via pass@k and a 3-stage LLM-judge pipeline.
external_memory_evidence: Agents interact with Android emulators by reading observational information (screenshots, UI hierarchies) and executing actions (taps, swipes, text input).
task_format_metric: pass@k protocols + staged 3-stage LLM-as-judge (MemGUI-Eval) across 7 hierarchical metrics
example_length: 3 other:attempts (multi-attempt trials per task (pass@k, k=3) used to assess cross-session/long-term learning) | 2 tasks (tasks per mirror pair (paired task design for cross-task learning transfer))
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] The paper explicitly defines memory for mobile GUI agents in two tiers: short-term (in-session) memory, which temporarily retains contextual information during task execution, and long-term (cross-session) memory, which accumulates experience from each interaction (success or failure) into persistent, transferable knowledge that improves efficiency across tasks over time.
evidence_span: ♠ Long-term (cross-session) memory accumulates experience from each interaction, whether successful or failed, forming reusable skills and knowledge... This memory is persistent, transferable, and aims to improve long-term efficiency across tasks.

description_authors_words: We introduce WorldPrediction, a video-based benchmark for evaluating world modeling and procedural planning capabilities of different AI models.
description_summary: Given initial and final visual world states, models must discriminate the correct action or correctly ordered action sequence from counterfactual distractors, testing high-level (not low-level motor) procedural planning.
task_format_metric: discriminative accuracy (choosing the correct action / action sequence among counterfactual distractors)
example_length: 3–10 steps (number of high-level action steps T per procedural-planning instance)
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] Prior procedural-planning evaluation is typically constrained to a short window of only 3-4 steps; WorldPrediction-PP instead evaluates 'long-horizon' procedural planning by extending the number of high-level action steps T up to 10 (T ∈ {3,...,10} for most source datasets, vs. the standard 3-4).
evidence_span: WorldPrediction-PP further extends the evaluation to procedural planning over extended temporal horizons, in contrast to existing benchmarks that typically focus on short spans of only 3-4 steps (Chang et al., 2020).

description_authors_words: We introduce a benchmark for coworker agents built around multi-turn multi-day tasks, a stateful sandboxed service environment whose state evolves between turns, and rule-based verification
description_summary: 100 multi-day office-coworker tasks across five stateful sandboxed services (email, calendar, filesystem, knowledge base, spreadsheet) whose state changes between turns independent of the agent, scored by 1537 deterministic post-execution checkers.
external_memory_evidence: executed against five stateful sandboxed services (filesystem, email, calendar, knowledge base, spreadsheet) and scored by 1,537 deterministic Python checkers over post-execution service state
task_format_metric: rule-based deterministic checker score (weighted score) + strict Task Success rate
example_length: 2–6 days (in-universe working days (turns) spanned per task) | 48–71 actions (tool calls per task (mean, across models))
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' anywhere (confirmed by full-text search); instead it defines its own precise vocabulary of 'turn' = one in-universe working day, with tasks spanning two to six turns/days, and explicitly distinguishes this from the legacy term 'stage'.
evidence_span: In this paper one turn is exactly one in-universe working day. A two- to six-turn task therefore spans two to six in-universe working days, and the agent receives one wake-up message at the start of each turn.

description_authors_words: We introduce GrowOVER , a set of dynamic QA and dialogue benchmarks that evaluate both retrievers and generators by annotating the evidence text and introducing a challenging dialogue task.
description_summary: Open-domain QA and dialogue benchmark periodically regenerated from fresh Wikipedia snapshots, testing whether a retrieval-augmented LM's answers keep pace with continuously evolving evidence over time.
external_memory_evidence: GrowOVER provides the evidence text along with the gold answers, which can be used to evaluate the retriever.
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
task_format_metric: QA F1/accuracy + dialogue generation BLEU, tracked over time as knowledge changes
example_length: 3–4 turns (turns per GrowOVER-Dialogue instance)
what_instead_if_absent: paper never uses 'long-horizon'/'long-term'; it frames its contribution entirely in Continual Knowledge Learning (CKL) terms of unchanged/changed/new knowledge over time
evidence_span: Our goal is to evaluate the retention of unchanged knowledge, the updating of changed knowledge, and the acquisition of new knowledge, aligning with the objectives of CKL.

description_authors_words: we introduce Knowledge Update Playground (KUP), an automatic pipeline for simulating realistic knowledge updates reflected in an evidence corpora. KUP's evaluation framework includes direct and indirect probes to both test memorization of updated facts and reasoning over them.
description_summary: After continued pretraining on a corpus of simulated real-world knowledge updates (beyond simple entity substitution), models are probed directly for memorized new facts and indirectly for reasoning that depends on them.
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
task_format_metric: direct probing (memorization MCQ) + indirect probing (reasoning MCQ / free-form QA via LLM judge)
example_length: 5 other:evidence_documents (news articles generated per knowledge-update pair (evidence corpus per example))
what_instead_if_absent: paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term'; it frames its contribution purely around continued pre-training on 'knowledge updates' and memorization-vs-reasoning probing
evidence_span: Large language models (LLMs) encode vast amounts of pre-trained knowledge in their parameters, but updating them as real-world information evolves remains a challenge.

description_authors_words: To evaluate this capability, we develop a four-phase protocol and two benchmarks in embodied manipulation and online shopping
description_summary: Two benchmarks (embodied manipulation, online shopping) with a four-phase protocol testing whether an agent learns a new user's preferences from scratch and adapts when those preferences later drift, via per-user memory.
external_memory_evidence: We therefore adopt standard dense-retrieval memory backends—a portable SQLite note store and a FAISS-based vector index—behind a shared API to keep the implementation simple and easily reproducible.

example_length: 120 tasks (scenarios per user across all 4 phases in the embodied-manipulation benchmark (30 scenarios/phase x 4 phases)) | 180 tasks (scenarios per user across all 4 phases in the online-shopping benchmark (45 scenarios/phase x 4 phases))
what_instead_if_absent: 'long-horizon sequential decision-making' and 'long-horizon sequential tasks' are used as unexamined given descriptors of the setting (a user corresponds to a sequence of tasks), without a stated task-count or duration threshold distinguishing it from shorter settings
evidence_span: We simulate long-horizon sequential decision-making, where each user corresponds to a sequence of tasks and each new interaction depends on the agent's accumulated preference memory.

description_authors_words: We synthesize a unique episodic memory benchmark, free from contamination, and release open source code and datasets to assess LLM performance across various recall and episodic reasoning tasks.
description_summary: Synthetic long narratives (default, sci-fi, news domains) embed events with who/what/when/where detail; the benchmark tests recall and reasoning over these episodic events via QA.
task_format_metric: F1-score on episodic-event recall/reasoning QA
example_length: 100000–100000 tokens (length of the standard evaluation book (single long-context episode) tested, ranging 10k-100k tokens) | 1000000 tokens (length of an additional scalability book (2000 chapters) generated to test beyond 100k tokens)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper defines 'episodic memory' itself in detail (via a cue/trace/event formalism grounded in Tulving's cognitive-science framework) but only uses 'long-term' in passing, to describe human memory generically, without pinning down what counts as long-term for its own benchmark
evidence_span: This transient nature of LLMs' memory contrasts sharply with human episodic memory, which allows for the long-term storage and retrieval of detailed experiences across an entire project or even lifespan.

description_authors_words: We introduce OSWorld 2.0, a benchmark of 108 long-horizon computer-use workflows across everyday and professional tasks, designed to capture complex and challenging real-world phenomena.
description_summary: An agent operates a real desktop OS end-to-end on 108 long (median 1.6-hour, ~318-tool-call) workflows spanning streaming interaction, cross-source reasoning, and stateful user profiles, scored by task completion.
external_memory_evidence: Agents must preserve state across desktop applications, web services, files, messages, and prior records over hundreds of steps, while handling

evidence_span: First, it must be long-horizon: its difficulty should come from interdependent workflow structure rather than repetition or concatenated subtasks.

description_authors_words: we introduce GameWorld, a benchmark designed for standardized and verifiable evaluation of MLLMs as generalist game agents in browser environments.

evidence_span: Puzzles test logical reasoning and long-horizon planning in discrete state spaces.

description_authors_words: we introduce a benchmark named CLMEEval, which consists of two datasets, i.e., CoNaLa-Edit (CNLE) with 21K+ code generation samples and CodeSearchNet-Edit (CSNE) with 16K+ code summarizati...
description_summary: Tests knowledge-editing methods on LLMs-for-code by measuring whether a single edit correctly fixes erroneous code-generation or code-summarization knowledge without breaking unrelated behavior, over two code-editing datasets.

example_length: 30.42 tokens (mean length of the editing target per instance (CNLE, generalization split)) | 57.35 tokens (mean length of the editing target per instance (CSNE, generalization split))

description_authors_words: We curate a more comprehensive temporal KE dataset with both knowledge update and knowledge injection examples for KE performance benchmarking.
description_summary: Temporal knowledge-editing dataset combining knowledge-update and knowledge-injection examples, used to compare parameter-efficient fine-tuning against locate-and-edit methods on multi-hop QA after time-sensitive edits.

description_authors_words: we first introduce the continual document learning (CDL) task for KILTs and build a novel benchmark dataset named KILT++ based on the original KILT dataset for evaluation.

description_authors_words: this paper proposes a comprehensive benchmark, RefuteBench, covering tasks such as question answering, machine translation, and email writing... to assess whether models can positively accept feedback in form of refuting instructions and whether they can consistently adhere to user demands throughout the conversation

description_authors_words: we propose a multi-level benchmark TIME, designed for temporal reasoning in real-world scenarios.

description_authors_words: we introduce SpecBench, a benchmark comprising 30 systems-level programming tasks ranging from short horizon tasks like building a JSON parser to ultra long horizon tasks like building an entire OS kernel from scratch.

description_authors_words: we also introduce Time-LongQA, a novel benchmark dataset based on real-world corporate annual reports, designed to test temporal reasoning across evolving knowledge.

description_authors_words: we introduce LOCA-bench (a benchmark for LOng-Context Agents). Given a task prompt, LOCA-bench leverages automated and scalable control of environment states to regulate the agent's context length.

task_format_metric: failure rate (cross-domain leakage / memory-induced sycophancy) via LLM-judge
example_length: 10–16 other:stored memories (number of long-term-memory items included per benchmark sample)
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] conversational assistants retain user-specific information across conversation sessions to support personalization and continuity, and the paper explicitly names this capability 'long-term memory'
evidence_span: These conversational assistants, relying on large language models (LLMs), retain user-specific information across conversation sessions to support personalization and continuity; we refer to this capability as long-term memory.

description_authors_words: PhysicianBench comprises 100 long-horizon tasks adapted from real consultation cases between primary care and subspecialty physicians, with each task independently reviewed by a separate panel of physicians.
description_summary: Tests LLM physician agents on 100 long-horizon clinical workflows (diagnosis, prescribing, treatment planning) executed via real EHR APIs across 21 specialties, averaging 27 tool calls per task, scored against fine-grained checkpoints.
external_memory_evidence: Concretely, we use the open-source HAPI FHIR JPA server  ( Smile CDR, 2024 ) backed by a persistent H2 database.
task_format_metric: checkpoint-based pass rate (execution-grounded + LLM-judged) across 670 fine-grained checkpoints
example_length: 27 actions (average tool calls per task) | 6.7 other:checkpoints (average checkpoints per task (670 checkpoints / 100 tasks))
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] long-horizon, composite clinical workflows are contrasted against prior medical-agent benchmarks that test only static knowledge recall, single-step atomic actions, or action intent without verifiable execution; PhysicianBench instead requires long-horizon, multi-step agent behavior spanning information retrieval, reasoning, action execution, and documentation
evidence_span: Existing medical agent benchmarks primarily focus on static knowledge recall, single-step atomic actions, or action intent without verifiable execution against the environment. As a result, they fail to capture the long-horizon, composite workflows that characterize real clinical systems.

description_authors_words: we introduce RepliBench, a suite of evaluations designed to measure autonomous replication capabilities... covering four core domains: obtaining resources, exfiltrating model weights, replicating onto compute, and persisting on this compute for long periods.
description_summary: 20 task families (86 tasks) testing whether an LLM agent can autonomously obtain compute resources, exfiltrate model weights, redeploy itself, and persist running for long periods, scored via pass@10.
task_format_metric: pass@1 / pass@10 aggregated across a capability tree of task families
what_instead_if_absent: the paper uses 'long-term' once, generically, to describe LLM agents 'making long-term plans and carrying out actions that would take humans several hours of work' (citing other work), and separately defines a 'Persistence' capability (surviving long-term via faster self-propagation than compute shutdown) without giving a threshold for what counts as long-term
evidence_span: Large language model agents (LLM agents) are increasingly capable of complex software engineering tasks, making long-term plans and carrying out actions that would take humans several hours of work.
scope_flag: RepliBench targets autonomous-replication SAFETY capability (an AI system's ability to obtain compute/money/weights and persist/spread copies of itself), evaluated as a capability tree of largely independent task families rather than as retention or use of a persistent memory store across sessions. Its 'Persistence' sub-capability ('surviving in the wild long-term by spreading to new compute faster than old compute is shut down') is about infrastructure survival, not memory-content retention, so its fit to the long-term-memory/long-horizon-execution charter is weaker than most other records in this shard.

description_authors_words: we introduce InnovatorBench, a benchmark-platform pair for realistic, end-to-end assessment of agents performing Large Language Model (LLM) research.
description_summary: Agents run 20 end-to-end LLM-research tasks (data construction, loss/reward design, scaffold building) in a long-horizon research environment, graded on runnable-artifact correctness and output quality.
task_format_metric: final/best task score plus execution time (hours), across 20 LLM research tasks
example_length: 36–36 hours (max time for the strongest agent to complete a task) | 11 hours (average time to reach best performance across models on InnovatorBench)
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] 'Horizon' is operationalized in the paper's own benchmark-comparison table as the time the agent takes to reach its best score; InnovatorBench tasks require the strongest agent up to 36 hours, with agents averaging over 11 hours to reach best performance
evidence_span: Horizon refers to the time the ReAct-based Agent takes to reach its best score. ML-Bench doesn't report this result.

description_summary: Agents given a system-prompt goal are exposed to competing environmental pressures over very long contexts (100,000+ tokens), measuring how much their behavior drifts from the original objective over time.
venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
task_format_metric: goal-adherence tracking over extended token budgets (goal-drift detection)
example_length: 100000 tokens (length of a single evaluation episode/context in the hardest setting (tokens over which goal adherence is tracked))
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] The paper does not use the term 'long-horizon' itself, but operationalizes sustained/extended agent operation via a token-length threshold: the best agent 'maintains nearly perfect goal adherence for more than 100,000 tokens' in its hardest evaluation setting, treating that scale as the boundary of extended autonomous operation.
evidence_span: we demonstrate that while the best-performing agent (a scaffolded version of Claude 3.5 Sonnet) maintains nearly perfect goal adherence for more than 100,000 tokens in our most difficult evaluation setting, all evaluated models exhibit some degree of goal drift.

description_summary: Real-time simulator (per its title) for evaluating long-term dialogue understanding in conversational agents; no abstract, cached text, or curated hint is available to specify its task format.
what_instead_if_absent: the shard's abstract field is empty; only the title is available, and it uses 'Long-Term Dialogue Understanding' without any definition
evidence_span: DialSim: A Real-Time Simulator for Evaluating Long-Term Dialogue Understanding of Conversational Agents

description_authors_words: we propose the Fine-Grained Visual Knowledge Editing (FGVEdit) benchmark, designed to evaluate the accuracy and effectiveness of multi-modal editing at a granular level.
description_summary: Tests whether a knowledge-editing method can precisely modify one entity's visual attributes within an image containing multiple interacting entities, without disturbing the unrelated entities' knowledge.
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
task_format_metric: editing accuracy/effectiveness at granular (entity-level) scope within images
what_instead_if_absent: the paper frames its contribution around fine-grained, visual, multi-entity knowledge editing; it never invokes or defines 'long-term'/'long-horizon'
evidence_span: we introduce a visual-oriented, fine-grained multi-modal knowledge editing task that targets precise modifications in images containing multiple interacting entities

description_summary: Evaluates seven existing model-editing algorithms for mitigating stereotype bias across three scenarios (single edit, sequential edits, cross-sentence generalization); a benchmarking study rather than a released benchmark dataset.
task_format_metric: bias-mitigation effectiveness and generalization across seven editing algorithms
what_instead_if_absent: the paper frames the work around model editing for debiasing and sequential-editing degradation, not long-horizon or long-term memory duration
evidence_span: Sequential editing highlights the robustness of SERAC (Mitchell et al. 2022b), while internal editing methods degenerate with the number of edits.
scope_flag: paper benchmarks seven EXISTING model-editing algorithms on debiasing; it does not appear to introduce a new named dataset/benchmark artifact of its own

description_authors_words: our study introduces MLaKE (Multilingual Language Knowledge Editing), a novel benchmark comprising 4072 multi-hop and 5360 single-hop questions designed to evaluate the adaptability of knowledge editing methods across five languages
description_summary: Multi-hop and single-hop QA over Wikipedia fact chains in English, Chinese, Japanese, French, and German, testing whether knowledge-editing methods generalize edits across languages.
task_format_metric: free-form and multiple-choice QA accuracy across knowledge-editing baselines
what_instead_if_absent: paper's axis of difficulty is multilinguality and multi-hop reasoning depth, not duration/session count; 'long-horizon'/'long-term' terminology does not appear
evidence_span: neglecting the complexities presented by multilingual contexts and multi-hop reasoning

description_authors_words: we introduce CookBench, a benchmark for long-horizon planning in complex cooking scenarios.
description_summary: An embodied agent in a Unity-based kitchen simulator must first parse an ambiguous user cooking request, then execute a long, fine-grained sequence of physical actions to fulfill it.
external_memory_evidence: we also provide the agent with a manually curated database of scene object and tool information (including weights, initial relative positions, and supported operations), as well as our spatial knowledge graph derived from a 3D semantic map
task_format_metric: intention recognition accuracy + embodied task success/HITL expert-comparison score
example_length: 120 steps (average number of high-level action steps per task (Embodied Interaction stage))
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] Existing embodied-planning benchmarks are short-to-medium horizon (e.g. ALFRED's average task length is only ~12 steps), which the authors say is insufficient to stress-test long-term memory, complex reasoning, and multi-task scheduling; CookBench instead targets 'ultra-long' sequences, with tasks averaging 120 steps.
evidence_span: For example, the average task length in ALFRED is only around 12 steps, which is insufficient to rigorously test an agent’s long-term memory, complex reasoning, and multi-task scheduling capabilities.

description_authors_words: we introduce T1, a tool-augmented, multi-domain, multi-turn conversational dataset specifically designed to capture and manage inter-tool dependencies across diverse domains.
description_summary: Multi-turn tool-use dialogues across nine domains requiring an agent to plan around dependent API calls, using a short/long-term cache to decide whether to reuse or recompute prior results.
external_memory_evidence: We introduce a data caching mechanism that enables T1-Agent to reuse the outputs of earlier tool calls when handling subsequent user requests. This reduces redundant computation and improves response efficiency in multi-turn interactions. After each user turn, any search results retrieved by a tool are cached for potential reuse in later turns. The save_to_cache tool is used to store these results.
task_format_metric: tool call F1 + parameter matching F1 across multi-turn dialogues
example_length: 6.0–9.0 turns (average turns per dialogue, single-domain settings (range across the four single domains)) | 9.7–11.3 turns (average turns per dialogue, multi-domain settings)
what_instead_if_absent: T1 uses 'long-term memory' only as the name of one tier of its caching mechanism ('an integrated caching mechanism for both short- and long-term memory'), never stating a threshold (e.g. a duration, turn count, or cache-lifetime rule) that distinguishes what counts as long-term versus short-term within the cache.
evidence_span: T1 enables rigorous evaluation of agents' ability to coordinate tool use across nine distinct domains (4 single domain and 5 multi-domain) with the help of an integrated caching mechanism for both short- and long-term memory, while supporting dynamic replanning-such as deciding whether to recompute or reuse cached results.

description_authors_words: we introduce Stark, a large-scale long-term multi-modal conversation dataset that covers a wide range of social personas in a multi-modality format, time intervals, and images
description_summary: Tests long-term multi-modal image-sharing dialogue by requiring generation of persona-appropriate, contextually consistent images and text across sessions spanning realistic time intervals.
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
task_format_metric: human evaluation (Likert) + dialogue-to-image retrieval
example_length: 4–6 sessions (sessions per episode (after data-cleaning filter))
what_instead_if_absent: the paper repeatedly calls its data 'long-term multi-modal conversation' and contrasts it with prior work's 'singular sessions,' but never states a duration/session-count threshold for what makes a conversation 'long-term'; the term is used as an unexamined given throughout.
evidence_span: existing works focus on (1) image-sharing behavior in singular sessions, leading to limited long-term social interaction, and (2) a lack of personalized image-sharing behavior.

description_authors_words: VideoCAD is a large-scale synthetic dataset consisting of over 41K annotated video recordings of CAD operations, generated using an automated framework for collecting high-fidelity UI action data from human-made CAD designs.
description_summary: 41K annotated CAD-operation videos with time horizons up to 20x longer than prior UI datasets, used both to train UI-action models and as a VQA benchmark testing spatial reasoning over long CAD interaction videos.
external_memory_evidence: We model CAD construction as a sequential decision process, where an agent observes UI frames and predicts low-level actions to recreate a target 3D model.
task_format_metric: action sequence prediction accuracy (command/parameter accuracy, Chamfer distance) + VQA accuracy
example_length: 186 actions (UI actions per task (Time Horizon, Table 1))
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] Time Horizon is operationalized in the paper's own comparison table as the number of UI actions required per task; VideoCAD is explicitly noted as having 'the longest time horizon-4x that of the next closest dataset (WebLinx)'.
evidence_span: We compare dataset complexity across five metrics: # Samples - total number of samples; Time Horizon - number of UI actions per task... As shown in Table 1, VideoCAD stands out across multiple dimensions. It features the longest time horizon-4 x that of the next closest dataset (WebLinx)

description_authors_words: we propose a new task formulation of the information updating task that only requires the provision of an unstructured updating corpus and evaluates the performance of information updating on the generalizability to question-answer pairs pertaining to the updating information.
description_summary: Tests whether LLMs updated on an unstructured corpus of recent news can generalize the new facts to held-out question-answer pairs, using datasets built from March-April 2023 news and Natural Questions.
venue: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
task_format_metric: factual consistency score (0-1) + QA accuracy on Replay Data and NQ Val
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-term' or 'long-horizon' anywhere (confirmed by full-text search); it frames its problem entirely as continual fine-tuning / information updating with a replay buffer to mitigate forgetting, evaluated via single-turn QA over updated facts.
evidence_span: Continual fine-tuning and knowledge editing approaches display limited generalization ability... existing continual fine-tuning approaches focuses on aligning LLMs with human preferences instead of incorporating new information.

description_authors_words: we introduce Odysseys: a benchmark of 200 long-horizon web tasks derived from real world browsing sessions evaluated on the live Internet
description_summary: 200 long, multi-site web-browsing workflows (e.g. cross-domain comparisons, multi-service trip planning) run live on the internet, graded by fine-grained rubrics rather than binary pass/fail.
task_format_metric: rubric-based LLM-judge scoring (avg. rubric score + perfect/binary success) + Trajectory Efficiency (rubric score per step)
example_length: 6.1–12 other:rubric_items (graded rubric items per task (average)) | 272.3–387 words (task instruction length in words (average)) | 1.9–3 other:categories (SimilarWeb fine-grained categories touched per task (average))
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] long-horizon web tasks are defined by contrast against 'short, single-site tasks that frontier models are approaching saturation on': long-horizon tasks are 'multi-site workflows' requiring 'sustained context and cross-site reasoning over potentially hours of browsing', with difficulty formally assigned by step count and domain spread (easy: <=5 steps/<=3 domains; medium: 6-8 steps or 4+ domains; hard: exceeding both)
evidence_span: Existing web agent benchmarks have largely converged on short, single-site tasks that frontier models are approaching saturation on. However, real-world web use consists of long-horizon, multi-site workflows... Difficulty is assigned by step count and domain spread: easy (<=5 steps, <=3 domains), medium (6-8 steps or 4+ domains), hard (exceeding both).

description_authors_words: we introduce the Legal Knowledge Update BEnchmark, i.e. LeKUBE, which evaluates knowledge update methods for legal LLMs across five dimensions.
description_summary: Legal-domain knowledge-editing benchmark testing whether methods can correctly update a legal LLM's statutory knowledge across five dimensions, addressing the length and nuance of legal regulations that open-domain editing benchmarks ignore.
external_memory_evidence: For the retrieval corpus, we use all statutes and judicial interpretations mentioned above from before and after the knowledge update as the retrieval corpus, prefixing statute names with "previous version of" or "latest version of" for differentiation. Each version of each statute is treated as a document to be retrieved, totaling 110,750 documents.
task_format_metric: true/false + multiple-choice question accuracy (update correctness + locality)
example_length: 114 other:characters (average length of one updated statute (pre-update, Chinese characters)) | 3.6 other:questions-per-statute (average number of true/false questions per updated statute)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-horizon'/'long-term'; it frames its contribution as the scalability and complexity of LEGAL knowledge editing (updating lengthy statute text, editing multiple chapters simultaneously) rather than duration or session-based memory.
evidence_span: Complexity of Legal Regulations: Legal regulations are typically more detailed and complex than the entity names in the general domain... it poses a significant challenge to existing knowledge update methods.

description_authors_words: we construct MEMENTO, an end-to-end two-stage evaluation framework comprising single-memory and joint-memory tasks.
description_summary: Embodied household agents must recall personally-meaningful object semantics and prior user behavioral routines, individually and jointly, to plan personalized object-rearrangement actions.
external_memory_evidence: we design a hierarchical knowledge graph-based user-profile memory module that separately manages personalized knowledge, achieving substantial improvements on both single and joint-memory tasks.
task_format_metric: task success rate / percent-complete score (single-memory vs joint-memory tasks)
example_length: 2 other:episodic-memories (distinct prior episodic memories synthesized per joint-memory task)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper frames its own contribution entirely via 'episodic memory', 'personalized knowledge', and 'memory utilization' across past interactions; 'long-term'/'long-horizon' appear in the text only when summarizing other papers' methods in the related-work section, never as the paper's own defining term.
evidence_span: To provide personalized assistance, agents must understand user instructions and conduct task planning by leveraging personalized knowledge retained from previous interactions—especially episodic memory, which enables the recall of specific events grounded in time and space

description_authors_words: we introduce Personalized Deep Research Bench (PDR-Bench), the first benchmark for evaluating personalization in DRAs. It pairs 50 diverse research tasks across 10 domains with 25 authentic user profiles...yielding 250 realistic user-task queries
description_summary: 250 user-task queries pairing 50 open-ended research tasks across 10 domains with 25 realistic user profiles, testing whether a deep-research agent personalizes its report via a joint alignment/quality/reliability score.
task_format_metric: PQR framework: Personalization Alignment, Content Quality, Factual Reliability
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never defines 'long-horizon'/'long-term' for its own construct; it frames personalization scope via 'dynamic personalized contexts' built from longitudinal memory snippets and conversational interactions collected 'over a period', without stating how long that period is or how many interactions it comprises.
evidence_span: To complement these explicit personas with dynamic context, we employed professional annotators simulate the daily interactions of these collected personas through a phone APP. Over a period, they were instructed to: 1) Record naturalistic memory snippets... This longitudinal data captures each user's evolving interests, habits, and implicit preferences.

description_authors_words: we introduce ToolQA-D, a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the impact of tool variability.
description_summary: Tests whether an LLM agent can keep invoking tools correctly after their APIs (names, parameters, response formats) change over time, rather than in a static tool environment.
task_format_metric: Task success/answer accuracy under API-name/parameter/response-format changes
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' (not found in the targeted read); it frames its scope entirely as 'tool variability' / 'dynamic environment' (APIs changing in name, parameters, or response format over time)
evidence_span: In alignment with real-world scenarios, we define the dynamic environment as everything excluding the LLM agent.

description_authors_words: we present WikiFactDiff, a dataset that describes the evolution of factual knowledge between two dates as a collection of simple facts divided into three categories: new, obsolete, and static.
description_summary: Tests factual-update algorithms on Wikidata facts that changed between two snapshot dates, via cloze-test accuracy across insertion, replacement, and removal update scenarios.
venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
task_format_metric: cloze-test accuracy of factual knowledge-update algorithms
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term'; it frames the task as 'factual update' between two knowledge-base snapshots
evidence_span: The factuality of large language model (LLMs) tends to decay over time since events posterior to their training are unknown to them.

description_authors_words: we propose a novel benchmark framework based on interactive fiction games, featuring dynamically branching storylines with complex reasoning structures... each choice triggers cascading dependencies across multi-turn interactions.
description_summary: Interactive-fiction benchmark with branching storylines where an LLM must track cascading consequences of earlier choices, tested both with immediate feedback and with self-directed backtracking after failure.
task_format_metric: correct-decision rate / task success across branching story paths (Immediate Feedback vs Self Recovery modes)
example_length: 6 other:chapters (chapters in the interactive-fiction narrative dataset) | 80 episodes (branching story paths evaluated per model across both task modes)
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] 'Long-term' is one of the comparison dimensions the paper defines for benchmarking LTM: many decisions require recalling events or facts introduced a few turns earlier, as opposed to 'Multi-turn', which just requires the task to unfold over many turns
evidence_span: Long-term : Many decisions require recalling events or facts introduced a few turns earlier.

description_authors_words: We introduce ATM-Bench, the first benchmark for multimodal, multi-source personalized referential Memory QA.
description_summary: Tests multimodal personal-memory QA requiring resolution of personal references, multi-evidence reasoning across images/videos/emails, and handling conflicting evidence, over roughly four years of a user's private records.
external_memory_evidence: In experiments, we implement 5 state-of-the-art memory systems along with a standard RAG baseline and evaluate variants with different memory ingestion, retrieval, and answer generation techniques.
task_format_metric: QA accuracy with human-annotated ground-truth memory evidence
example_length: 226–933 days (average time span between the earliest and latest evidence items required to answer a single question (ATM-Bench-Hard split)) | 1.6 other:evidence items (average evidence items per query (standard ATM-Bench split)) | 6.3 other:evidence items (average evidence items per query (ATM-Bench-Hard split))
what_instead_if_absent: the paper reports concrete scale figures (approximately four years of personal memory data; per-question evidence spans averaging 226 days, max 933 days) but never states a sentence pinning down what duration or session count counts as 'long-term' for this benchmark
evidence_span: Personalized AI assistants must recall and reason over long-term user memory, which naturally spans multiple modalities and sources such as images, videos, and emails.

description_authors_words: we introduce REGEN Reviews Enhanced with GEnerative Narratives, a new dataset extending the Amazon Product Reviews with rich user narratives.
description_summary: Amazon Product Reviews extended with generated user narratives, testing whether a model can produce personalized, narrative-style recommendation explanations grounded in a user's interaction history, scored by an LLM rater.
task_format_metric: automated LLM-rater evaluation of generated narrative quality vs. reference
example_length: 50–50 other:items (user-item interaction sequence length (truncated to the most recent N items))
what_instead_if_absent: The paper uses 'long-term user preferences' once, to describe the intent of its 'Narrative Generation from Aggregate Context' task (capturing a comprehensive narrative of the user's overall experience), but never states a threshold (e.g., a minimum interaction-sequence length) that would define what makes preferences 'long-term'.
evidence_span: Narrative Generation from Aggregate Context: Generate natural language output T(S) corresponding to the entire interaction history. This task aims to capture long-term user preferences and generate a comprehensive narrative reflecting the user's overall experience.

description_authors_words: we introduce FindingDory, a new benchmark for long-range embodied tasks in the Habitat simulator. FindingDory evaluates memory-centric capabilities across 60 tasks requiring sustained engagement and contextual awareness in an environment.
description_summary: An embodied agent in the Habitat simulator must recall logged navigation and manipulation events from an earlier multi-day exploration to complete new instructions, across 60 procedurally extendable tasks.
external_memory_evidence: In these scenarios, an agent receives logs of prior interactions in indoor environments and must complete navigation, pick, and place instructions.
task_format_metric: task success rate (navigation to correct target based on memory recall)
example_length: 400–3500 other:frames (frames per episode during experience collection) | 2–11 steps (pick-and-place interactions per episode)
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] long-horizon embodied control is defined by contrast with prior VLM work on 'short-term or static tasks... which do not require sustained memory usage'; long-horizon control instead requires agents to 'integrate observations over time, recall past experiences, and act accordingly within their environment.'
evidence_span: However, most existing VLM applications focus on short-term or static tasks, such as image captioning or Visual Question Answering (VQA), which do not require sustained memory usage. Extending these models to long-horizon embodied control introduces new challenges: embodied agents must integrate observations over time, recall past experiences, and act accordingly within their environment.

description_authors_words: This paper introduces Agents' Last Exam (ALE), a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on long horizon, economically valuable, real world tasks with verifiable outcomes
description_summary: Over 1,000 expert-authored professional tasks spanning 55 non-physical industries, continuously expanding, scored by deterministic checks and rubrics; hardest tier sees under 1% full pass rate.
task_format_metric: deterministic checks + structured rubrics (per-task normalized score in [0,1])
example_length: 10 other:minutes (typical wall-clock duration of one agent run on one ALE task instance ('tens of minutes to hours')) | 400000–1000000 tokens (context-window truncation limit enforced during long-horizon agent runs)
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] long-horizon authentic workflows are contrasted with the 'task units that are easier to collect' used by prior work, namely 'shorter computer-use tasks, synthetic environment construction, or purely question-answering setups'; long-horizon here means real, economically valuable, multi-step professional work sourced from real software and organizational contexts.
evidence_span: long-horizon authentic workflows are expensive to collect because they must be sourced from real software and organizational contexts. Prior work often adopts task units that are easier to collect, whether shorter computer-use tasks, synthetic environment construction, or purely question-answering setups.

description_authors_words: we present $\texttt{BLUR}$: a benchmark for LLM unlearning that provides more realistic scenarios of forget-retain overlap.
description_summary: LLM-unlearning benchmark with deliberately overlapping forget/retain query sets and relearning-attack datasets, testing whether unlearning methods truly erase targeted knowledge rather than exploiting easy forget-retain separation.
task_format_metric: forget-quality vs retain-quality accuracy on combined forget/retain queries, incl. relearning-attack robustness
what_instead_if_absent: paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term'; it is framed entirely around machine unlearning, forget-set/retain-set overlap, and relearning attacks
evidence_span: Machine unlearning has the potential to improve the safety of large language models (LLMs) by removing sensitive or harmful information post hoc.
scope_flag: This benchmark evaluates machine UNLEARNING (deliberate removal of targeted knowledge for safety) rather than long-term memory retention, updating, or long-horizon execution; it fits the charter only loosely via the 'forgetting' construct, and the paper never frames itself in long-horizon/long-term terms at all.

description_authors_words: we introduce StreamEQA, the first benchmark designed for streaming video question answering in embodied scenarios.
description_summary: MLLMs answer perception/interaction/planning questions about 156 long embodied videos as they stream in, with questions requiring backward, real-time, or forward reasoning over a specific temporal window.
task_format_metric: QA accuracy on timestamped streaming video QA
example_length: 67.5 other:seconds (average video duration per example)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-term' or 'long-horizon'; it defines its scope via the 'Streaming' dimension (backward/real-time/forward reasoning over incrementally acquired observations) and reports average video length (67.5s) instead.
evidence_span: an agent must maintain situational awareness of its environment, comprehend the interactions with surrounding entities, and dynamically plan actions informed by past observations, current contexts, and anticipated future events.

description_authors_words: By organizing GitHub issues into chronologically ordered sequences that reflect natural repository evolution, SWE-Bench-CL enables direct evaluation of an agent's ability to accumulate experience, transfer knowledge across tasks, and resist catastrophic forgetting
description_summary: Reorders SWE-Bench Verified's GitHub issues into chronological per-repository sequences to test whether a coding agent accumulates experience and transfers knowledge across issues instead of forgetting, via continual-learning transfer/forgetting metrics.
external_memory_evidence: an interactive, LangGraph - based evaluation framework augmented with a FAISS - backed semantic memory module
task_format_metric: continual-learning metrics (accuracy, forgetting, forward/backward transfer, CL-F1/CL-Fbeta)
example_length: 34.1–50 tasks (average number of chronologically-ordered issues/tasks per repository sequence (one continual-learning trajectory))
what_instead_if_absent: the paper defines its object via 'continual learning' (accumulating experience, transferring knowledge, resisting catastrophic forgetting across a chronological task stream) and uses 'long-term' only once, as an aspirational vision statement rather than an operational or contrastive definition of the benchmark's difficulty axis
evidence_span: The long-term vision is to cultivate coding agents that not only address immediate software engineering challenges but also continuously augment their expertise and reliability through sustained interaction with evolving codebases and task streams, truly embodying the principle of "agents that continuously learn."

description_authors_words: We introduce MEMTRACK, a benchmark designed to evaluate long-term memory and state tracking in multi-platform agent environments.
description_summary: Chronologically interleaved timelines of Slack, Linear, and Git events test an agent's memory acquisition, selection, and conflict resolution while tracking organizational state, scored beyond plain QA accuracy.
external_memory_evidence: LLM+Mem0 : In this method, the agent consists of a LLM with an additional within-agent Mem0 -based [ 19 ] memory component that exposes an additional set of its own tools, for example, search_memory() , store_memory() , get_memories() , to the agent.
task_format_metric: Correctness / Efficiency / Redundancy via LLM-judge, plus tool-call entropy metrics
example_length: 39.9–115 other:events (events per instance timeline (Per-Instance Event Count)) | 4010–11100 tokens (total tokens in one instance's event timeline (Event Tokens)) | 878–3049 hours (timespan covered by one instance's timeline (Timeline Span in Hours))
length_unit_families: stored memory items; tokens / text length; wall-clock time
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] long-term/long-horizon memory demand is operationalized by the timespan a chronologically platform-interleaved event timeline covers, which averages 878 hours and reaches up to 3049 hours (about 4 months) in the hardest instances
evidence_span: our timelines span 878 hours on average, stretching across 3000 hours in some cases.

description_authors_words: we present Persona2Web, the first benchmark for evaluating personalized web agents on the real open web, built upon the clarify-to-personalize principle, which requires agents to resolve ambiguity based on user history rather than relying on explicit instructions.
description_summary: Web agents must infer a user's implicit preferences from their browsing/task history to resolve ambiguous instructions on the real open web, scored by a reasoning-aware personalization framework.
external_memory_evidence: The retriever receives history queries from the planner and searches for relevant entries in the user history.
