evidence_span: Continuous Evolution Environment. The agent operates within a persistent, stateful environment where modifications from each task persist into the next. This compels the agent to maintain the long-term health of the codebase, as early technical debt or latent bugs can accumulate and impede future progress.

description_authors_words: We introduce MTBBench, an agentic benchmark simulating MTB-style decision-making through clinically challenging, multimodal, and longitudinal oncology questions.
description_summary: Clinician-validated oncology tumor-board simulation requiring multimodal, multi-agent reasoning over a patient's evolving longitudinal record, testing integration of time-resolved and conflicting clinical evidence.
external_memory_evidence: To support reasoning over temporal sequences of clinical events, we introduce two tools that provide external biomedical knowledge for answering longitudinal questions more accurately: a literature search tool and a pharmacological knowledge base.
task_format_metric: clinician-validated QA accuracy across multimodal and longitudinal oncology tracks
example_length: 5 other:files (files (genomic/clinical-timeline documents) associated per patient case, longitudinal track) | 4.6 other:questions (questions per patient case, longitudinal track)
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] Longitudinality is defined as patient histories unfolding over multiple timepoints with temporally ordered updates; operationally, the agent interacts across multiple turns where retrieved files do not persist by default (they 'remain accessible only within the current turn') and must be actively re-requested at future turns, with an evolving timeline cumulatively summarizing patient history
evidence_span: Longitudinality : Patient histories unfold over multiple timepoints, with temporally ordered updates. [...] The agent may issue a request R_t... which remain accessible only within the current turn. Namely, they do not persist across turns. However, any file... may be re-requested at a future turn t', simulating realistic constraints in clinical workflows where information must be actively re-acce

description_authors_words: we introduce a comprehensive dataset ActMemEval to evaluate agent reasoning capabilities in logic-driven scenarios, moving beyond the fact-retrieval focus of existing memory benchmarks
description_summary: Tests whether an agent's retrieved memory supports causal and counterfactual reasoning over implicit constraints, not just fact retrieval, using a structured causal/semantic graph built from dialogue history.
external_memory_evidence: ActMem transforms unstructured dialogue history into a structured causal and semantic graph.
task_format_metric: logic-driven memory-utilization accuracy (compared against LongMemEval/LoCoMo baselines)
example_length: 67.25 sessions (sessions per dialogue history (average)) | 120000 tokens (tokens per dialogue history (average)) | 2.48 sessions (evidence sessions per question (average))
what_instead_if_absent: the paper uses 'long-term interactions' as an unexamined premise throughout (echoing cited memory-system literature) and never states a duration/session threshold that defines it; instead it demonstrates its dataset is 'structurally denser' than two related benchmarks (more sessions, longer contexts, more scattered evidence) via a comparison table
evidence_span: Memory management is essential for LLM agents in long-term interactions.

description_authors_words: we first propose a pipeline to construct MMEVOKE, a benchmark for evaluating LMMs' ability in multimodal evolving knowledge injection.
description_summary: 9,422 samples across 159 subtypes testing whether multimodal models can absorb newly injected evolving (image+text) knowledge without degrading their existing general capabilities.
external_memory_evidence: Here, we focus on the knowledge injection performance of Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation (MM-RAG) on LMMs. Three retrieval strategies are employed: Text-Only (retrieving candidate documents only based on textual features), Image-Only (retrieving candidate documents only based on visual features), UniIR  ( Wei et al., 2024 ) (retrieving candidate documents based on multimodal features).
task_format_metric: QA accuracy on injected evolving knowledge + general-capability degradation metrics
example_length: 95.7–386 words (average length of one evolving-knowledge instance (the injected fact/update text))
what_instead_if_absent: the paper frames its entire contribution as 'evolving knowledge injection' and capability-degradation tracking; it never uses the terms 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' anywhere in the cached text
evidence_span: Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) store vast amounts of pretrained knowledge but struggle to remain aligned with real-world updates, making it difficult to avoid capability degradation when acquiring evolving knowledge.

description_authors_words: we propose LCMP, the first Long-Context MLLM Personalization evaluation benchmark.
description_summary: Tests whether a multimodal LLM can track how a personalized visual concept (e.g., a specific pet) changes over a long conversation history and generate responses reflecting those temporal/persistent variations.
external_memory_evidence: As a strong baseline for LCMP, our framework equips the personalized MLLM assistant with a double-memory architecture : one memory stores static and universal personalized knowledge, while the other monitors dynamic contextual information throughout the interaction.
task_format_metric: multi-turn VQA accuracy (simple/hard questions) over historical vision-language dialogues
example_length: 14 other:dialogues (historical dialogues per personalized concept (~420 dialogues / 30 concepts))
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] long-term attributes refer to relatively stable properties that persist with the personalized concept (e.g., pet's name, favorite food), contrasted with short-term attributes that vary dynamically
evidence_span: The long-term attributes refer to relatively stable properties that persist with the personalized concept (e.g., pet's name, favorite food).

description_authors_words: We introduce ConstraintRot, a benchmark of long-horizon agent scenarios with deterministic tool-call grading, and measure compaction-induced violations across seven model families
description_summary: Long-horizon agent scenarios with an explicit safety constraint test whether context compaction/summarization silently drops the constraint from memory, letting the agent later perform a prohibited tool call; graded by deterministic violation detection.
task_format_metric: deterministic violation-rate grading (prohibited tool-call detection), control vs. compaction
example_length: 5900–20000 tokens (session token length before/at compaction in a ConstraintRot scenario)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper names its benchmark 'a benchmark of self-contained long-horizon agent scenarios' as a background descriptor, but its own formal scenario structure is defined in terms of a policy turn + benign task turns + trigger request, not a duration/step threshold for 'long-horizon' itself
evidence_span: ConstraintRot, a benchmark of self-contained long-horizon agent scenarios that pairs a governance constraint with a later prohibited request, graded deterministically by detecting the prohibited effect in the agent’s tool call.

description_authors_words: We introduce CoffeeBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in a long-horizon multi-agent economy composed of heterogeneous firms.
description_summary: 90-day simulated coffee supply-chain economy where an LLM-controlled roaster negotiates and transacts with five reference-agent firms (farmers, roasters, retailers), scored by cumulative net income under long-horizon multi-agent competition.
external_memory_evidence: Each agent maintains an internal operational state, including cash balance, inventory, accounts receivable, and accounts payable.
task_format_metric: cumulative net income over simulated run
example_length: 90 days (simulation horizon per CoffeeBench run)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper repeatedly uses 'long-horizon' and 'extended periods' as background motivation (citing prior long-horizon business-management benchmarks) but never states a day/step criterion that pins down what qualifies as long-horizon for its own task
evidence_span: As LLM agents become capable of increasingly long-horizon tasks, evaluating their performance in economic systems is becoming increasingly important.

description_authors_words: Due to the lack of publicly available datasets specifically tailored for our novel task, we compiled a new dataset and an evaluation benchmark.
description_summary: Evaluates a method for jointly unlearning outdated/problematic facts, integrating new facts, and preserving unrelated knowledge, scored by accuracy separately on unlearn, update, and retain data splits.
task_format_metric: accuracy on unlearn/update/retain datasets + Arc Easy benchmark
what_instead_if_absent: the paper's definitional apparatus concerns a three-component loss objective (unlearn/update/retain datasets), not a long-horizon/long-term temporal framing; those terms never appear in the sections searched
evidence_span: x_i^unl ∈ D^unl, x_i^upd ∈ D^upd, and x_i^rtn ∈ D^rtn represent sequences of tokens from the unlearning, update, and retain datasets, respectively.

description_authors_words: we introduce the Multilingual Knowledge Editing Benchmark (MKEB), a novel dataset comprising 12 languages and providing a complete evaluation framework
description_summary: Knowledge-editing dataset spanning 12 languages, testing whether an edit made in one language propagates correctly to the same fact expressed in the other 11 languages.
what_instead_if_absent: The paper frames its contribution entirely as multilingual knowledge editing (propagating factual updates across languages) without any 'long-term'/'long-horizon' framing or terminology.
evidence_span: we focus on multilingual knowledge editing (MKE), which requires propagating updates across multiple languages.

description_authors_words: We introduce RetailBench, a data-grounded simulation benchmark for evaluating tool-using LLM agents in single-store supermarket operation.
description_summary: Thousand-day-scale supermarket simulation where an agent manages pricing, replenishment, and inventory as a partially observable process, testing sustained long-horizon decision coherence against a privileged oracle policy.
external_memory_evidence: In this environment, agents must manage pricing, replenishment, supplier selection, shelf assortment, inventory aging, customer feedback, external events, and cash-flow constraints.
task_format_metric: final net worth / sales outcomes vs. a privileged oracle policy over the evaluation horizon
example_length: 180 days (days per agent evaluation run (the horizon over which one agent operates in a single episode))
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] agents are evaluated over a 180-day evaluation horizon inside an environment explicitly designed to support thousand-day-scale simulations, i.e. long-horizon is operationalized as sustained multi-hundred-day decision-making
evidence_span: We evaluate seven contemporary LLMs under representative agent frameworks over a 180-day evaluation horizon and compare them with a privileged oracle policy.

description_authors_words: we develop CHED -- a benchmark designed to evaluate the context robustness of KE methods.
description_summary: Tests whether a knowledge-edited fact still holds when the query is preceded by conversational context that would normally cue the model's original, pre-edit answer.
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
task_format_metric: editing success rate under preceding-context conditions
what_instead_if_absent: the paper frames its contribution around context-robustness of edits (preceding utterances triggering retrieval of stale knowledge), not around a long-horizon/long-term duration construct
evidence_span: In real-world applications, however, preceding contexts often trigger the retrieval of the original knowledge and undermine the intended edit.

description_authors_words: we introduce EverGreenQA, the first multilingual QA dataset with evergreen labels, supporting both evaluation and training.
description_summary: Multilingual QA dataset labeled by whether each question's answer is evergreen (stable) or mutable (changes over time), testing if models explicitly or implicitly recognize a question's temporal stability.
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
task_format_metric: evergreen/mutable classification accuracy (verbalized judgments + uncertainty signals); downstream QA accuracy with a trained classifier (EG-E5)
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] questions are evergreen (answers remain stable over time) or mutable (answers change).
evidence_span: whether they are evergreen (answers remain stable over time) or mutable (answers change).

description_authors_words: we introduce TRAVELER, a novel synthetic benchmark dataset that follows a Question Answering paradigm and consists of questions involving temporal references with the corresponding correct answers
description_summary: Tests whether a model can resolve explicit, implicit (relative-to-speech-time), and vague temporal references via QA, with vague-reference ground truth established through human surveys.
task_format_metric: QA accuracy across explicit/implicit/vague temporal-reference categories, by event-set length
example_length: 5–100 other:events (event-set length per example (number of prior events a model must reason over), swept across levels)
what_instead_if_absent: The paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term'; instead its controlled scale variable is 'event set length' (number of prior events a system must reason over, varied from 5 to 100), and it reports that 'performance clearly deteriorates with larger event set length' -- this stands in for a long-horizon/long-term framing without ever naming it as such.
evidence_span: performance clearly deteriorates with larger event set length and when temporal references get less explicit.

description_authors_words: we introduce a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on their ability to handle interaction with streaming data.
description_summary: Diagnostic benchmark testing whether an MLLM agent can answer ad-hoc queries about a streaming video by grounding responses in historical, present, and future observations despite evidence arriving asynchronously relative to the query.
external_memory_evidence: All memory entries are stored in a FAISS  [ 27 ]  vector database to enable efficient similarity-based retrieval.
task_format_metric: Multiple-choice QA accuracy + mean temporal response offset (seconds)
example_length: 22–90 other:minutes (average duration of source videos per query (range 6-90 minutes))
what_instead_if_absent: paper frames its own challenge as 'Query-Evidence Asynchrony' rather than defining long-horizon/long-term; 'long-horizon' appears only when citing other memory-augmented video systems in related work
evidence_span: We frame this challenge as Query-Evidence Asynchrony, where user queries and their supporting evidence typically arrive asynchronously in the streaming setting.

description_authors_words: we systematically develop a suite of new evaluation methods
description_summary: Not itself a stable benchmark: introduces negative-example evaluation methods showing that reported model-editing success is largely an artifact of shortcut exploitation rather than real knowledge integration.
task_format_metric: Edit success rate (Efficacy, exact-token match) and Hallucination score under positive/negative test variants
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses the terms 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' at all; it frames its contribution purely around sequential/batch knowledge editing and negation-based evaluation
evidence_span: We follow AlphaEdit to consider the scenario that combines both sequential editing and batch editing: For each dataset, we edit 2000 samples, with 100 samples per edit batch.

description_summary: The same emotional-intelligence test scenario is paired with different injected user memory profiles to see whether a model's emotional interpretation and advice shift based on a user's socioeconomic or demographic profile.
external_memory_evidence: We used Facebook AI Similarity Search (FAISS) to retrieve top 3 relevant sentences per question.
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
task_format_metric: emotional-intelligence test accuracy (STEU/STEM) conditioned on an injected user profile, plus flip-rate and advantaged-vs-disadvantaged bias-influence gap
what_instead_if_absent: the paper asserts that LLMs 'now incorporate sophisticated long-term memory that persists across conversations' as unexamined background motivation, then moves directly to studying bias from injected user profiles without ever defining long-term/long-horizon
evidence_span: As personalized AI systems increasingly incorporate long-term user memory, understanding how this memory shapes emotional reasoning is critical.
scope_flag: The paper studies bias from a single static user-profile/persona injected once into the system prompt (one-shot personalization of an existing emotional-intelligence test), not retention, retrieval, or update of memory across sessions; 'long-term memory' is invoked only as motivating background in the intro, and the one experiment that manipulates context length (Appendix G) uses a LongBench-style long-context stress test, not a persistent memory mechanism.

description_authors_words: We also introduce Ledger-QA, a diagnostic benchmark for long-horizon state tracking over accumulated updates.
description_summary: Diagnostic QA benchmark requiring aggregation over accumulated updates (e.g., summed transaction totals) from a stream, testing long-horizon latent-state tracking independent of any specific memory-agent architecture, stratified by session horizon.
external_memory_evidence: We introduce Unified Memory Agent (UMA) for a one-to-many setting: query-agnostic external memory is constructed once from a stream and reused across multiple future QA sessions.
task_format_metric: Exact Match / F1 / ROUGE-L / LLM-as-judge accuracy on latent-state aggregation questions (e.g. summed transaction totals), stratified by session horizon
example_length: 2–500 other:updates (session/update horizon H per Ledger-QA test instance (accumulated bookkeeping updates before the query))
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] test difficulty is stratified by 'session horizon' H, the number of accumulated updates/sessions before the query, with H ranging over {2, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 100, 500}; larger H is the paper's long-horizon regime, requiring continuous aggregation of a latent state (e.g. summed transactions) rather than local span retrieval
evidence_span: The test set is stratified by session horizon (H ∈ {2, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 100, 500}).

description_authors_words: we release MansionWorld, a dataset of over 1,000 diverse buildings ranging from hospitals to offices, alongside a Task-Semantic Scene Editing Agent that customizes these environments using open-vocabulary commands to meet specific user needs.
description_summary: Embodied agents perform object-retrieval and navigation tasks spanning multiple floors of generated multi-story 3D buildings, testing cross-floor long-horizon spatial planning as task difficulty scales with floor count.
external_memory_evidence: All logical checks (e.g., path connectivity) and geometric planning (e.g., surface area calculation) are executed directly against this JSON structure and an external Asset Metadata Database (Asset DB).
task_format_metric: task success rate / progress score (object-retrieval + navigation) across single-, two-, and four-floor settings
example_length: 1–4 other:floors (floors per building environment in the evaluated long-horizon task settings (single-floor, two-floor, four-story)) | 1–10 other:floors (buildable floors per generated building (framework capability, MANSION generation))
what_instead_if_absent: the paper uses 'long-horizon' pervasively (long-horizon tasks, long-horizon planning, long-horizon spatial planning/memory) but never states a step-count or duration threshold; the closest operational proxy is floor count (single-floor vs. two-floor vs. four-story settings), which the paper does not explicitly equate with 'long-horizon' as a defined quantity
evidence_span: Many critical applications, ranging from package delivery in offices, supply transport in hospitals, to multi-step chores at home, are inherently long-horizon and at the building scale.

description_authors_words: We introduce HeroBench, a benchmark for evaluating long-horizon, hierarchical planning and structured reasoning in a complex RPG-inspired virtual world
description_summary: RPG-style virtual-world planning benchmark requiring hundreds-to-thousands of actions in one executable plan (equipment selection, multi-level crafting/resource dependencies), scored via simulation-verified success and fine-grained progress metrics.
task_format_metric: task success rate + progress score (simulation-verified)
example_length: 40–937 actions (environmental actions required to complete a task, mean at difficulty level 1)
what_instead_if_absent: uses 'long-horizon' as an unexamined given describing the planning task, characterized only by scale (hundreds to thousands of actions) rather than a stated definition of the term itself
evidence_span: yet their ability to carry out robust long-horizon planning under realistic constraints remains insufficiently evaluated

description_authors_words: we introduce PIRA-Bench (Proactive Intent Recommendation Agent Benchmark), a novel benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on continuous, weakly-supervised visual inputs.
description_summary: Long, noisy screenshot trajectories with interleaved multithreaded tasks test whether a multimodal agent detects actionable user intents and offers proactive recommendations without an explicit instruction.
external_memory_evidence: The framework features a dedicated memory module that dynamically records and tracks ongoing multitasking states and specific user profile contexts.
task_format_metric: Average Intent F1 + Normalized False Positive Score (final score = product)
example_length: 32 steps (sequential screenshots per trajectory (average))
what_instead_if_absent: uses 'long-horizon' to describe noisy, multithreaded real-world screen trajectories without giving a definition or threshold; the only quantified property offered is trajectory screenshot count (unrelated to a stated horizon definition)
evidence_span: Real-world screen activity is rarely linear; it consists of long-horizon trajectories fraught with noisy browsing, meaningless actions, and multithreaded task-switching.

description_authors_words: We introduce AFTER, a benchmark of 382 realistic enterprise tasks spanning six professional roles and 22 procedural skills, designed to evaluate how skills transfer across tasks, roles, and model backbones.
description_summary: Agents build reusable procedural skills from enterprise task experience and are tested on whether those skills transfer to new tasks, new job roles, and different model backbones.
external_memory_evidence: Skills are stored as versioned SKILL.md artifacts with YAML metadata and
task_format_metric: M1 (full-pass accuracy) and M2 (pass-rate) via pytest verification, transfer splits across roles/models
what_instead_if_absent: never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term'; frames its object of study as procedural-memory 'transfer' across tasks, roles, and model backbones instead of horizon length
evidence_span: We introduced AFTER, a benchmark for evaluating procedural memory through transfer across tasks, roles, and model backbones.

description_authors_words: we introduce the Non-linear Task Multi-turn Dialogue (NTM) benchmark, specifically designed to assess model performance in long-horizon, non-linear scenarios.
description_summary: Multi-turn dialogues with branching, non-linear topic shifts and instruction refinements, testing whether a model maintains coherence and completes tasks when conversation history forms a tree rather than a flat sequence.
external_memory_evidence: By constructing trees based on navigational intent (e.g., instruction refinement, topic switching) and retrieving coherent paths instead of isolated nodes, our approach preserves the logical continuity requisite for complex, long-horizon tasks.
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
task_format_metric: Task Completion Rate (TCR) + Average Context Tokens (ACT)
example_length: 10–25 turns (turns per dialogue (four difficulty bands))
what_instead_if_absent: uses 'long-horizon, non-linear scenarios' as an unexamined descriptor of dialogues with topic shifts and instruction refinements; contrasts only with 'short (<10 turns), linear' prior datasets, without stating a threshold for its own benchmark
evidence_span: specifically designed to assess model performance in long-horizon, non-linear scenarios

description_authors_words: We introduce SynthTools, a fully LLM-based pipeline spanning the entire lifecycle: environment generation, simulation, validation and task construction.
description_summary: Not a fixed benchmark but an LLM-driven pipeline that generates diverse, verifiable tool-use environments and multi-step task trajectories at scale (73,883 tools, 6,800 environments, 79,925 tasks) for agent training/evaluation.
task_format_metric: task success (verifiable tasks) via generated trajectories; downstream tool-use benchmark gains
what_instead_if_absent: uses 'long-horizon tasks/reasoning' as an unexamined descriptor of what tool-use agents must solve, and states the pipeline exposes 'control over difficulty, length, trajectory composition' as tunable parameters, but never states what length/step count counts as long-horizon
evidence_span: For agentic systems to use external tools to solve complex, long-horizon tasks, we need a large set of diverse and controllable tool-use environments.

description_authors_words: we develop an application-level testbed based on the open-source strategy game "Unciv", which has millions of active players, to enable researchers to build a "data flywheel" for studying human-like agents in the "digital players" task.
description_summary: Testbed built on the open-source 4X strategy game Unciv, evaluating whether an LLM agent can handle long-term numerical planning, diplomacy, and human-like social negotiation while playing against or with humans.
external_memory_evidence: Memory Module. As shown in Figure 2 , the memory module primarily stores data generated from the agent’s interactions, including short-term memory, which consists of the most recent 20 lines of dialogue and actions, and long-term memory, which is generated by the reflection of skill usages and recent decisions.
task_format_metric: skill success rate + human-likeness ratings
example_length: 100 other:turns (order-of-magnitude game length ('hundreds of turns', spanning several hours to days of real time)) | 20 messages (short-term memory window (most recent lines of dialogue/actions retained verbatim))
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] the memory module distinguishes short-term memory, consisting of the most recent 20 lines of dialogue and actions, from long-term memory, generated by reflection on skill usages and recent decisions and stored for later retrieval
evidence_span: the memory module primarily stores data generated from the agent's interactions, including short-term memory, which consists of the most recent 20 lines of dialogue and actions, and long-term memory, which is generated by the reflection of skill usages and recent decisions

description_authors_words: We introduce SAKE, the first benchmark for editing perceptual auditory attribute knowledge in large audio-language models (LALMs), which requires modifying acoustic generalization rather than isolated facts.
description_summary: Tests knowledge-editing methods on audio-language models by requiring edits to generalize across acoustic perceptual attributes, scored on reliability, generality, locality, and portability under single and sequential edits.
task_format_metric: reliability/generality/locality/portability scores under single and sequential knowledge editing
example_length: 10 steps (editing instances per sequential-editing sequence) | 5–5 steps (maximum evaluated edit gap (steps between when an edit is applied and evaluated))
what_instead_if_absent: The paper never frames its editing-persistence dimension as 'long-term' or 'long-horizon'; instead it operationalizes durability through an editing 'gap' — the number of subsequent edit steps between when an edit is applied and when it is evaluated, capped at five.
evidence_span: To measure how long an edit remains effective under subsequent edits, we define the gap as the number of editing steps between when an edit is applied and when it is evaluated

description_authors_words: we propose BESPOKE, the realistic benchmark for evaluating personalization in search-augmented LLMs... by collecting authentic chat and search histories directly from humans, and diagnostic, by pairing responses with fine-grained preference scores and feedback
description_summary: Real human chat and search histories are used to test whether a search-augmented LLM personalizes its answers to that person's revealed intent, scored with fine-grained human preference ratings and diagnostic feedback.
external_memory_evidence: To measure history retrieval performance, we designate oracle histories using an LLM as ground truth and evaluate the retriever's performance
task_format_metric: fine-grained preference scores + diagnostic feedback from human annotators
example_length: 73.5 sessions (search sessions per user (average)) | 24.3 sessions (chat sessions per user (average)) | 4.3–53 turns (turns per chat session (average))
what_instead_if_absent: The paper uses 'long-term' only to describe the data-collection process itself ('long-term, deeply engaged human annotation' over a three-week period) rather than to define what counts as a long history or long horizon for the personalization task; user histories vary in size (session counts) but no threshold distinguishes 'long-term' from 'short-term' histories.
evidence_span: The benchmark is constructed through long-term, deeply engaged human annotation, where human annotators contributed their own histories, authored queries with detailed information needs, and evaluated responses with scores and diagnostic feedback.

description_authors_words: we introduce MyEgo, the first egocentric VideoQA dataset designed to evaluate MLLMs'ability to understand, remember, and reason about the camera wearer.
description_summary: 541 long egocentric videos with 5K personalized questions about 'my things/activities/past', testing whether an MLLM can track and recall facts about the specific camera-wearer rather than generic video content.
task_format_metric: multiple-choice/open-ended QA accuracy
example_length: 9.2 other:minutes (video length (average)) | 9.3 tasks (questions per video (average))
what_instead_if_absent: The paper uses 'long-range memory'/'long-term memory' only as an unexamined closing motivation ('highlight the crucial role of ego-grounding and long-range memory'); its actual defined construct is 'ego-grounding' — understanding 'me', 'my things', 'my activities', and 'my past' in first-person video — not a length threshold for what counts as long-term.
evidence_span: These findings collectively highlight the crucial role of ego-grounding and long-range memory in enabling personalized QA in egocentric videos.

description_authors_words: we introduce Causal-LoCoMo, a causally annotated benchmark derived from long conversational data, where each example contains a user request, a structured memory bank, useful memories, irrelevant distractors, and synthetic harmful memories.
description_summary: Tests whether a memory-selection method picks genuinely useful stored memories over topically-similar but stale, irrelevant, or synthetically harmful ones, scored by answer quality and rejection of misleading memories.
external_memory_evidence: Long-horizon LLM agents rely on persistent memory to support interactions across sessions, yet existing memory systems often retrieve context using semantic similarity or broad history inclusion, treating retrieved memories as uniformly useful.
task_format_metric: hybrid task score/success rate + useful-memory F1, bad-memory rejection, poisoned-memory adoption
example_length: 4.97 sessions (past LoCoMo sessions per Causal-LoCoMo example (derived: 432 sessions / 87 examples)) | 491 other:memory_entries (total memory-bank entries across the dataset (89 useful + 348 irrelevant + 54 harmful))
what_instead_if_absent: The paper uses 'long-horizon'/'long-term' pervasively as an unexamined given throughout (e.g. 'long-horizon LLM agents', 'reliable long-term memory'), inheriting the temporal scale from the LoCoMo dataset it is derived from, but never itself states a threshold, contrast baseline, or explicit definition of what makes an agent or its memory 'long-horizon'.
evidence_span: Long-horizon LLM agents rely on persistent memory to support interactions across sessions, yet existing memory systems often retrieve context using semantic similarity or broad history inclusion, treating retrieved memories as uniformly useful.

description_authors_words: We introduce the Factorio Learning Environment (FLE), based on the game of Factorio, that tests agents in long-term planning, program synthesis, and resource optimization
description_summary: LLM agents write Python code via a REPL to automate the factory-building game Factorio, tested on 24 fixed-resource lab-play tasks plus an unbounded open-play factory-growth task requiring long-horizon planning.
external_memory_evidence: a persistent coding environment for LLM agents to interact with the game through iterative program synthesis
task_format_metric: lab-play task success on fixed production targets; open-play production-score (PS) growth over steps
example_length: 5000 steps (environment steps per open-play episode used for plotting agent progress/reward) | 128 actions (environmental interactions after which agents still fail to coordinate more than six machines (lab-play))
what_instead_if_absent: repeatedly uses 'long-term planning'/'long-horizon planning' as a target capability without ever defining a threshold or scale that makes a task 'long-term'; the closest concrete anchor is an observation that models still fail 'even after 128 environmental interactions'
evidence_span: We introduce the Factorio Learning Environment (FLE), based on the game of Factorio, that tests agents in long-term planning, program synthesis, and resource optimization.

description_authors_words: we introduce VitaBench 2.0, a benchmark for evaluating personalized and proactive agent behavior in long-term user interactions.
description_summary: Temporally ordered task sequences per user, with preferences fragmented across heterogeneous interactions, test whether an agent extracts, uses, and updates personal preferences and proactively seeks missing information.
external_memory_evidence: To reflect realistic long-term interaction scenarios, we allow the agent to maintain an external memory module that stores and updates user-specific information over time.
task_format_metric: Avg@4 / Pass@4 task success under different memory configurations, plus separate proactive-behavior scoring
example_length: 14.6 tasks (tasks per user's temporally-ordered interaction sequence (average)) | 4–8 turns (user-assistant turns per task-oriented dialogue (typical))
what_instead_if_absent: uses 'long-term user interactions' repeatedly as the paper's framing (e.g. 'interactions are often long-term and fragmented across sessions') without ever giving a numeric threshold; the closest concrete anchor is that 'users have at least 10 tasks in their task sequences', a dataset-construction fact rather than a stated definition of 'long-term'
evidence_span: In realistic scenarios, interactions are often long-term and fragmented across sessions, making memory mechanisms essential for maintaining user representations.

description_authors_words: we introduce PillagerBench, a novel framework for evaluating multi-agent systems in real-time competitive team-vs-team scenarios in Minecraft.
description_summary: Teams of LLM agents compete head-to-head in real-time Minecraft matches against rule-based opponents, scored by points, sabotage, and win rate across multiple rounds of adaptive play.
external_memory_evidence: The multi-agent system object persists between episodes, enabling continuous learning.
