what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term'; its entire framing is about single-forward-pass, instantaneous knowledge internalization (hypernetwork-based document-to-weights adaptation) and conflict resolution at the level of one document/one question
evidence_span: Hypernetwork-based methods such as Doc-to-LoRA internalize a document into an LLM's weights in a single forward pass, but they fail systematically on conflicts

description_authors_words: This study proposes Tool-RoCo, a novel benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) in long-term multi-agent cooperation based on RoCo, a multi-robot cooperative benchmark.
description_summary: Multiple LLM-controlled robots cooperate on three multi-robot tasks (sorting, packing, cabinet arrangement) by treating other agents as callable tools, testing self-organized coordination across four autonomy paradigms.
task_format_metric: Tool-selection/parameter-filling accuracy plus cooperation/self-organization tool-usage ratios (CT%, SO%)
example_length: 10 turns (turns per episode, with up to 5 re-planning opportunities)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper repeatedly calls its setting 'long-term multi-agent cooperation'/'long-term interaction environments' as an unexamined qualifier, but never ties this to a threshold or contrast; the only concrete interaction-scale figures given (five episodes per task, up to ten turns per episode with up to five re-planning opportunities) are reported as experimental configuration, not connected back to a definition of 'long-term'
evidence_span: It remains unclear how LLMs can coordinate and self-organize with other agents in long-term tasks, limiting the evaluation of their autonomy.

description_authors_words: we introduce MineExplorer benchmark for evaluating open-world exploration capabilities of MLLM agents in Minecraft... we organize the benchmark around a ReAct-style capability formulation and compose atomic tasks into implicit multi-hop tasks.
description_summary: Minecraft open-world exploration benchmark composing filtered atomic tasks into implicit multi-hop tasks, scored by rule-based milestone and task success rates, targeting general exploration rather than game-specific knowledge.
external_memory_evidence: You have access to a local Minecraft wiki database with pre - fetched descriptions .
task_format_metric: rule-based milestone success rate (Milestone Success Rate) + task success rate, validated against human judgment
example_length: 1–4 other:hops (dependency-graph hops per composite benchmark instance) | 1800 steps (environment-step budget per benchmark instance (agent run capped at this many steps))
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] long-horizon exploration is contrasted with short-horizon exploration: models can handle many single-hop tasks (goal close to the visible environment) but fail once hidden prerequisites must be inferred and coordinated across longer trajectories spanning multiple hops (1-hop to 4-hop composite tasks)
evidence_span: Even the best models still fail on most multi-hop tasks, suggesting that current MLLM agents are not yet able to sustain long-horizon exploration in dynamic open worlds.

description_authors_words: We introduce OR-Space, a full-lifecycle workspace benchmark for evaluating industrial optimization agents across model construction, model revision, and grounded explanation.
description_summary: Tests operations-research agents across a full task lifecycle (build a solver model, revise it under changing requirements, explain it) using persistent multi-file workspaces of business documents, data, and solver outputs.
external_memory_evidence: Each OR-Space instance is represented as a persistent executable workspace containing business documents, structured data, optional code artifacts, solver outputs, and task-specific evaluators distributed across multiple interdependent files.
task_format_metric: solver-grounded pass/feasibility scoring for Build/Revise, grounded LLM-as-judge rubric (Exact Coverage, Reasoning, Grounding, Answer Quality, Hallucination Penalty) for Explain
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' at all; instead it frames its scope entirely via 'persistent multi-artifact workspaces' (files distributed across an executable environment) and a 'lifecycle-oriented' task setting (Build/Revise/Explain) as the two axes distinguishing it from one-shot OR benchmarks
evidence_span: Such settings abstract away two defining characteristics of real-world industrial OR workflows: (1) the workspace setting , in which agents must operate within persistent multi-artifact workspaces containing requirements, structured data, code artifacts, solver feedback, and stakeholder interactions; and (2) the task setting , in which agents must support multiple stages of the OR lifecycle rather
scope_flag: The paper never uses the terms 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' anywhere in the text; its 'persistent multi-artifact workspace' means a single instance's files (documents, data, code, solver output) are distributed across multiple interdependent files, not that state is carried across sessions or a long execution trajectory. The Revise task does carry a prior model forward across one revision step, but this is a two-stage lifecycle (Build then Revise/Explain), not a long-running or multi-session trajectory, so fit with this charter's long-horizon-execution / long-term-memory definitions is a stretch.

description_authors_words: we present FutureWorld, a live agentic reinforcement learning environment that closes the training loop between prediction, outcome realization, and parameter updates.
description_summary: Live prediction-market RL environment where an agent forecasts real-world event outcomes and is only rewarded once the outcome resolves later, testing delayed-credit learning from real-world feedback via calibration and Brier score.
task_format_metric: probabilistic prediction accuracy/Brier score/calibration (ECE), scored after delayed real-world outcome resolution
example_length: 1 days (delay between prediction time and the scheduled outcome-resolution attempt for training rollouts (daily cycle)) | 2 days (delay between a question's release and ground-truth retrieval for the FutureWorld daily benchmark)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never applies 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' to its own environment; the only occurrence of 'long-horizon' is in a cited reference title ('Reinforcement learning for long-horizon interactive llm agents'), and 'long-term memory' appears only describing a different related-work framework (Hermes). FutureWorld instead frames its own scope entirely via 'delayed-feedback' and a 'live, rolling stream' of daily-resolved questions
evidence_span: This proposed framework decouples prediction-time rollout collection from later outcome retrieval, reward backfilling, and policy update.

description_authors_words: we release human reference data and benchmarks to support future work on simulating human memory with language models.
description_summary: Runs classic psychology memory experiments (digit span, free recall, etc.) on both humans and LLMs, finding off-the-shelf LLMs remember far better than humans, and releases the resulting benchmark and human reference data.
external_memory_evidence: This agent explicitly implements a human-like working memory bottleneck via a key-value memory module.

what_instead_if_absent: 'long-horizon' is used only once, in background text describing where the broader field of agent-memory evaluation is heading ('evaluation has shifted toward long-horizon, multi-turn, and dynamic settings'), citing other benchmarks; the paper's own ten tasks are classic single-session psychology memory tests (digit span, narrative recall, etc.) bounded by short time limits (3-5 minutes reading, one-hour total session), not framed by the paper itself as long-horizon or long-term
evidence_span: As memory and retrieval improve, evaluation has shifted toward long-horizon, multi-turn, and dynamic settings that test whether agents can manipulate information over extended interactions

description_authors_words: to simulate scenarios with frequent knowledge updates, we constructed ConflictKG, a knowledge conflict QA benchmark
description_summary: QA benchmark simulating frequent knowledge updates, used to measure whether a decoding-time method resolves conflicts between a model's stored parametric knowledge and newer contextual evidence.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing
task_format_metric: QA accuracy under contrastive/dynamic decoding, separately reported for conflict and non-conflict scenarios
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' at all; it frames its scope purely via 'context-memory conflicts', i.e. static disagreement between a generated context passage and the model's parametric knowledge for a single question, with no session or duration dimension
evidence_span: Large language models accumulate extensive parametric knowledge through pre-training. However, knowledge conflicts occur when outdated or incorrect parametric knowledge conflicts with external knowledge in the context.
scope_flag: The paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' anywhere (confirmed by full-text search); each ConflictKG instance is a single-turn QA pair with one generated context passage (conflicting or non-conflicting with parametric knowledge), constructed from a Wikidata subgraph -- there is no session history, multi-turn structure, or persistent store being updated over time. It fits this charter's 'knowledge-update-conflict' construct only in the generic RAG-vs-parametric-knowledge-conflict sense, motivated by 'frequent knowledge updates' in the abstract, not by any multi-session or temporal-update mechanism.

description_authors_words: We also introduce MMA-Bench, a programmatically generated benchmark for belief dynamics with controlled speaker reliability and structured text-vision contradictions.

evidence_span: Memory-augmented LLM agents increasingly underpin long-horizon interactive systems that must preserve and update user-specific context over time (Park et al., 2023; Guo et al., 2024).

description_authors_words: The benchmark combines auctions, hidden-offer trade challenges (TCs), bargaining, bluffing, opponent modeling, and resource allocation within a single long-horizon game lasting 50--60 turns.

description_authors_words: we introduce Mini Amusement Parks (MAPs), an amusement-park simulator designed to evaluate an agent's ability to model its environment, anticipate long-term consequences under uncertainty, and strategically operate a complex business

description_authors_words: we introduce EvoBrowseComp, an evolving benchmark of 400 English and 400 Chinese contamination-free complex questions synthesized via live-web traversal.

description_authors_words: We study this surface as deployment-time memorization, formulating agent memory as a privacy-utility frontier measured by Personalization Recall (PR) and Adversarial Extraction Rate (AER), and sweeping three memory-design knobs: summarization aggressiveness, retrieval breadth (k), and deletion mode.

description_authors_words: we introduce ALPBench, a Benchmark for Attribution-level Long-term Personal Behavior Understanding. Unlike item-focused benchmarks, ALPBench predicts user-interested attribute combinations, enabling ground-truth evaluation even for newly introduced items.

example_length: 274500–284700 tokens (context token length per user history instance, 1-year window (max observed, e.g. Apparel category)) | 1049–1147 other:interactions (average interactions per user (1-year history window, e.g. Pants category))

evidence_span: We propose attribute-level user interest prediction as a principled objective for evaluating personalized intelligence in LLMs, explicitly decoupling stable user preferences from transient real-time factors (e.g., popularity and platform dynamics) and focusing on long-term, inferable personalization signals.

description_authors_words: MREval, a fine-grained evaluation framework assessing four memory-driven abilities - Anchoring, Recalling, Bounding, and Enacting

description_authors_words: We introduce MemFail, a diagnostic benchmark that isolates the failure modes of modern LLM memory systems.

description_authors_words: we introduce SaaSBench, the first benchmark designed to explore the boundaries of AI agents in enterprise SaaS engineering. Spanning 30 complex tasks across 6 SaaS domains with 5,370 validation nodes

The second category ... placing higher demands on long-horizon planning, cross-file coordination, and system-level consistency

description_authors_words: we introduce SMDD-Bench, a challenging, multi-turn, long-horizon agentic benchmark consisting of 502 guaranteed-solvable task instances spanning 5 task types: 2D Pharmacophore Identification, Interaction Point Discovery, Scaffold Hopping, Lead Optimization, and Fragment Assembly.

what_instead_if_absent: cites 'long-horizon tasks' as prior-work motivation via a bare citation, without stating what makes a task long-horizon; the paper's own focus is the memory-commitment decision (persist/verify/clarify) at a single candidate-commitment moment, not on horizon length itself
evidence_span: LLM agents increasingly retain interaction history to personalize later behavior and support long-horizon tasks [1, 2].

description_authors_words: We introduce MerchantBench, a 365-day order-level simulation grounded in 98,843 real e-commerce product records and equipped with 26 tools for agent interaction.
description_summary: 365-day e-commerce seller simulation over 98,843 real product records where an agent must manage sourcing, pricing, and cash flow while delayed order outcomes force it to revisit and stay consistent with earlier decisions.
external_memory_evidence: The environment grounds a Product Catalog in 98,843 real e-commerce product records and converts demand into individual orders that progress through fulfillment and after-sales stages.
task_format_metric: business-outcome metrics + decision-trace analysis for Long-Term Coherence across a 365-day simulation
example_length: 365 days (simulated days per MerchantBench run) | 8760 steps (hourly simulation steps per run (365 days x 24 hours))
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] 'Long-Term Coherence' is defined as 'the capacity to preserve purposeful behavior across extended horizons while adapting decisions to accumulated evidence', operationalized as a 365-simulated-day, hourly-stepped (8,760-step) e-commerce simulation with delayed feedback and revisitable earlier decisions
evidence_span: Real-world deployments often require Long-Term Coherence, the capacity to preserve purposeful behavior across extended horizons while adapting decisions to accumulated evidence.

description_authors_words: We introduce SovereignPA-Bench, an executable benchmark for evaluating user-owned personal agents under evolving intent, platform mediation, privacy boundaries, consent constraints, evidence requirements, and burden tradeoffs.
description_summary: Personal agents face 120 sovereignty-stress scenarios testing whether they advance a user's evolving interests while respecting privacy, consent, and resistance to manipulative incentives, scored on multi-metric component scores.
task_format_metric: multi-metric sovereignty scoring (task, alignment, privacy, consent, evidence, manipulation, burden, auditability)
what_instead_if_absent: 'long-term memory' appears only inside one cited reference's title ('Augmenting language models with long-term memory'); the paper's own framing is entirely around 'user sovereignty' under 'evolving intent, platform mediation, and consent constraints', with no stated duration/scale criterion
evidence_span: Personal agents are becoming persistent user-owned intermediaries: they remember preferences, filter platform-mediated information, use tools, and negotiate with services.

description_authors_words: AgentCL constructs compositional streams where earlier sub-solutions, evidence, or workflows are intentionally reusable in later tasks, and contrasts them with naive streams where such reusability is not guaranteed
description_summary: Agents work through controlled task streams designed with deliberate cross-task reuse opportunities (versus naive streams without them), measuring transfer, stability, and generalization gains from non-parametric memory.
external_memory_evidence: MemProbe first retrieves a small set of relevant past experiences from memory using embedding-based similarity search over previously stored task descriptions.
task_format_metric: accuracy + Plasticity Gain / Stability Gain / Generalization Gain (PG/SG/GG) metrics
example_length: 40 tasks (tasks in the naive AgentBoard BabyAI-derived task stream) | 90 tasks (tasks in the naive AgentBoard ScienceWorld-derived task stream) | 300 tasks (tasks in the naive MMLU-Pro-derived task stream)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper motivates itself via 'long-term competence' and 'long-term agentic interactions' as unexamined premises ('intensive inference does not automatically compound into long-term competence'), then substitutes a different, precisely defined construct as its actual object of study: controlled compositional vs. naive task streams with explicit inter-task reuse relationships (Sec 3-4), rather than defining what duration or scale makes an interaction 'long'.
evidence_span: The fact that intensive inference does not automatically compound into long-term competence motivates the continual learning (CL) problem for language agents

description_authors_words: We introduce PM-Bench, a text-based benchmark for measuring prospective memory capabilities in modern LLM agents.
description_summary: Text-based simulated seven-day-week testbed (Virtual Week paradigm) where an agent must remember to perform deferred intentions at the right future cue while continuing an ongoing activity, scored by cue-triggered hit-rate F1.
task_format_metric: F1 score (hit rate on cue-triggered actions) + monitoring-cost accounting
example_length: 7 days (length of one PM-Bench scenario (simulated week)) | 80 steps (total time-anchored steps in one PM-Bench scenario (7 days x 10-13 steps/day))
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] PM-Bench increases long-horizon pressure in two ways. First, cross-day tasks are announced on an earlier day but become executable only when a cue appears later, so successful execution requires maintaining a deferred intention across multiple intervening steps and days. Second, explicit cancellation or rescheduling can revise a task's cue, time, or action text, forcing the model to update an existing intention instead of relying on the initial encoding.
evidence_span: PM-Bench increases long-horizon pressure in two ways. First, cross-day tasks are announced on an earlier day but become executable only when a cue appears later, so successful execution requires maintaining a deferred intention across multiple intervening steps and days.

description_authors_words: To evaluate the capability of existing agents on this task, we introduce MMG2Skill-Bench, the first benchmark designed for this problem.
description_summary: Tests whether an agent can convert noisy, human-oriented multimodal how-to guides into an executable, self-improving skill, evaluated across GUI control, gameplay, and card-play domains by task success and step efficiency.
external_memory_evidence: MMG2Skill initializes editable inference-time skills from public human-written guides and revises only the skill files from agent-visible trajectory diagnoses  ( Madaan et al., 2023 ) , without consuming benchmark scores.
task_format_metric: task success + step efficiency (mean displayed-attempt steps) under guide-to-skill learning
example_length: 10.08 steps (macro-average steps to complete a GUI-domain task (Vanilla baseline)) | 41.17 steps (macro-average steps to complete a Game-domain task (Vanilla baseline))
what_instead_if_absent: uses 'long-horizon tasks'/'long-horizon procedural work' repeatedly as generic motivation for why guide-to-skill learning matters, but never pins the term to a duration, step-count, or contrast that would define what qualifies as long-horizon.
evidence_span: Vision-language model (VLM) agents are increasingly expected to perform long-horizon procedural work in interactive environments, from operating software in desktop GUIs... to completing open-world game objectives... and playing rule-constrained card games.

description_authors_words: We introduce RECON (Reasoning over Extended Contexts with Obfuscated Narratives), a benchmark for evaluating compositional reasoning over long contexts
description_summary: 24 long case files (50k-100k tokens, criminal/medical/financial) testing six memory-intensive tasks -- multi-hop evidence chains, cascading fact invalidation, source-conflict resolution, counterfactual reasoning, and temporal constraints -- past mere fact-change detection to its downstream consequences.
external_memory_evidence: Supermemory is a cloud document-memory store with semantic search.
task_format_metric: accuracy on six memory-intensive tasks (multi-hop evidence chains, cascading invalidation, source conflict, counterfactual, temporal constraints, temporal fact retrieval)
example_length: 50000–100000 tokens (per-case-file context length)
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] RECON spans 24 case files across three domains (criminal, medical, and financial), each ranging from 50k to 100k tokens
evidence_span: RECON spans 24 case files across three domains (criminal, medical, and financial), each ranging from 50k to 100k tokens, and tests agents on six memory-intensive tasks.

description_authors_words: We introduce Egostream, a diagnostic benchmark for streaming episodic memory evaluation in egocentric vision.
description_summary: 2,250 questions over egocentric video, expanded via an Answer Validity Window into 8,528 recall evaluations from instant to ultra-long-term, testing whether streaming memory-management mechanisms distinguish true forgetting from world-state change.
external_memory_evidence: offloading ( OFFLOAD ), which preserves excess chunks on disk for retrieval at question time via cosine similarity
task_format_metric: recall accuracy across seven recall-regime windows (instant to ultra-long-term), unified streaming-MLLM harness
example_length: 30–480 minutes (lower bound of the 'Long-term' Answer Validity Window recall regime) | 8 hours (lower bound of the 'Ultra-long-term' Answer Validity Window recall regime)
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] Long-term recall regime: Window 30m-8h (Late Synaptic Consolidation). Ultra-long-term recall regime: Window >8h. Both derived from a seven-tier taxonomy (Instant 0s; Short-term 0-5s; Short-mid-term 5-30s; Mid-term 30s-3m; Mid-long-term 3m-30m; Long-term 30m-8h; Ultra-long-term >8h) grounded in memory-consolidation timescales from psychology.
evidence_span: Drawing on established memory consolidation timescales, application-oriented considerations, and empirical support in our data, we define seven recall regimes spanning a log-scaled progression. Table 3 reports the proposed recall regimes and terminology... Long-term 30m-8h Late Synaptic Consolidation... Ultra-long-term 8h+ Long-term.

description_authors_words: we introduce LikeBench, a multi-session, dynamic evaluation framework that measures likability across multiple dimensions by how much an LLM can adapt over time to a user's preferences to provide more likable responses.
description_summary: An LLM converses with a simulated user across multiple sessions and is judged, turn by turn, on whether it adapts tone, references, and knowledge to become more likable to that specific user over time.
task_format_metric: Per-dimension likability score (1-5) via simulated-user LLM judge, plus memory-recall accuracy
what_instead_if_absent: the paper only encounters 'long-term'/'very long-term' when citing other benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval) in its related-work table; its own contribution is framed via sessions S and turns T without ever defining what counts as 'long'
evidence_span: Evaluating very long-term conversational memory of llm agents.

description_authors_words: We introduce Momento, a benchmark for persistent agentic task completion in multi-session service environments, requiring agents to take consequential, tool-mediated actions while resolving temporal dependencies and evolving user goals across sessions.
description_summary: Multi-session service-agent benchmark where consequential tool-mediated actions in later sessions depend on evolving user goals from earlier ones, testing whether agents re-validate stale session history rather than trust it blindly.
external_memory_evidence: Long-term memory retrieves relevant prior sessions from a session database via LLM-generated SQL queries that jointly incorporate semantic matching, temporal constraints, and structural conditions.
task_format_metric: Task Success Rate and Pass Rate over persistent multi-session tool-mediated tasks
example_length: 3 sessions (prior sessions preceding the final evaluated session per task instance (K, as used in the main results of Table 1))
what_instead_if_absent: 'long-horizon human-agent interaction' and 'long-term multi-session interactions' recur as unexamined descriptive labels for the setting; the paper instead formally defines its scenario length via a per-task session count parameter K (K=3 used in main results) rather than defining what makes an interaction 'long-horizon'
evidence_span: highlighting a substantial gap between current agent capabilities and realistic long-horizon human-agent interaction

description_authors_words: we present a benchmark of 312 expert-validated, time-sensitive German statutory QA pairs spanning three categories: Post-Cutoff Amendment Questions, Pre-Amendment Questions, and Multi-Provision Pre-Amendment Questions
description_summary: Tests whether an LLM answering German statutory-law questions applies superseded rules after amendments (staleness) or wrongly prefers newer provisions over the historically correct one (recency bias), via expert-validated legal QA.
external_memory_evidence: We evaluate five LLMs by OpenAI, Anthropic and DeepSeek under four inference settings: Vanilla , Web-search , and two retrieval-augmented variants that enforce temporal validity via a fact date extraction and version filtering.
task_format_metric: LLM-as-judge outcome/reasoning/legal-basis/version correctness, validated against human experts
what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' (zero hits in full text); it frames its problem entirely via 'post-cutoff staleness' and 'recency bias' as named temporal failure modes
evidence_span: We study two temporal failure modes: post-cutoff staleness, where models apply superseded rules after legislative amendments, and recency bias, where models prefer newer provisions even when a historical version governs the fact pattern.

description_authors_words: we introduce \method{}, a dynamic evaluation environment that simulates a "trainee" agent continuously exploring a novel setting.
description_summary: Dynamic 'trainee'-agent environment (Trainee-Bench/EvoEnv) testing context-aware scheduling of streaming tasks, active exploration to reduce hallucination, and whether an agent distills generalizable strategies from repeated rule-based tasks over time.
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
task_format_metric: Success Rate and Checkpoint Score, measured daily within the simulation
example_length: 2 days (consecutive simulated days per continual-learning scenario (Day 1 / Day 2)) | 2–6 tasks (meta-tasks per scenario in the workload-stratification experiments (Table 3))
what_instead_if_absent: 'long-term' appears only in motivational asides ('long-term stability', 'long-term strategic evolution', 'long-term memory management') and in citations to other 'long-horizon' benchmarks, without the paper itself stating a threshold; its own construct is instead formalized as a scenario with deadline-distributed tasks and a two-day (Day 1/Day 2) continual-learning structure
evidence_span: To ensure long-term stability, agents must learn from prior experiences to prevent the recurrence of historical errors in subsequent scenarios

description_authors_words: We introduce alem, a JAX-based benchmark for open-ended multi-agent coordination built on Craftax-like dynamics.
description_summary: Teams of LLM agents must coordinate exploration, crafting, trading, and combat in a long-horizon open-ended survival world, scored by normalized episode return split into base-task and coordination reward.
external_memory_evidence: At each timestep, models receive a textual state containing recent observation-action history, teammate messages, a private scratchpad, and visible coordination constraints, together with explicit action affordances.
task_format_metric: Normalised episode return (Base%, Coord.%, Total%)
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] Long horizon means that success requires maintaining progress over extended trajectories, with rewards delayed by T timesteps where T is typically in the hundreds or thousands.
evidence_span: Long horizon means that success requires maintaining progress over extended trajectories, with rewards delayed by T timesteps where T is typically in the hundreds or thousands.

description_authors_words: we introduce PrecisionMemBench, an 89-case benchmark measuring precision, noise isolation, session latency, and belief mutability
description_summary: 89 cases isolate retrieval precision from answer quality, testing whether a memory system retrieves exactly the right stored belief rather than dumping its whole store to inflate apparent recall.
external_memory_evidence: Within a domain-specific belief store, semantic similarity may preserve broad subject-matter relevance without uniquely identifying the intended belief.
task_format_metric: Precision, noise isolation (drift score), session latency, belief mutability
example_length: 10 turns (turns per session test case (topic drifts across 8 unrelated turns, then returns to the original topic at turns 9 and 10))
what_instead_if_absent: 'long-term memory' appears only inside the paper's own goal statement ('to organize long-term memory rather than merely retrieve facts') and inside cited benchmark titles (LongMemEval, Mem0, Mnemis); the paper's own formal construct is the 'belief', an atomic typed unit of persistent context, not a definition of long-term/long-horizon itself
evidence_span: to organize long-term memory rather than merely retrieve facts, isolating

description_authors_words: we introduce Source-distributed Multimodal Memory Benchmark(SMMBench), which measures whether agents can retrieve, align, and compose multimodal evidence scattered across multiple sources rather than reason within a single curated context.
description_summary: 1,877 multiple-choice items grounded in 264 heterogeneous sources (chats, profiles, screenshots, tables, images, documents), testing whether an agent can retrieve and compose evidence scattered across independent sources rather than a single pre-assembled context.
task_format_metric: Multiple-choice accuracy / exact match across 5 task types
example_length: 831 turns (average turns per conversational source) | 45.43 turns (average turn-interval between pieces of relevant evidence within a conversational source) | 2.82 other:sources (average number of input sources required to answer one QA pair)
what_instead_if_absent: 'long-horizon'/'long interaction histories' appear only as descriptive labels (e.g. citing 'LifeSim: long-horizon user life simulator') or as a consequence of the design ('sustained tracking over long interaction histories'), without a stated threshold; the paper's own concrete anchor is the measured 831 turns per conversational source with evidence spaced every 45.43 turns
evidence_span: This design reduces shortcut solving from locally clustered clues and makes memory retrieval depend on sustained tracking over long interaction histories.

description_authors_words: We present AlphaEval, a production-grounded benchmark of 94 tasks sourced from seven companies deploying AI agents in their core business, spanning six O*NET (Occupational Information Network) domains.
description_summary: Evaluates complete commercial agent products (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) on real production tasks with implicit constraints and multi-modal fragmented inputs from seven companies, judged by domain experts and multi-paradigm rubrics.
external_memory_evidence: Environment Provisioning : Docker containers are instantiated with task input files
task_format_metric: Multi-paradigm rubric scoring (LLM-as-judge, reference-driven, formal verification), plus economic value grounding
example_length: 25.7 hours (average professional human labor hours per task (computed: 2,420 total hours / 94 tasks)) | 46 turns (average agent turns per task (Claude Code + Opus 4.6 configuration))
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] Long-horizon deliverables means outputs are complete professional artifacts—10-page investment reports, full-stack codebases, multi-visit clinical calculations—rather than short answers or code snippets.
evidence_span: long-horizon deliverables (outputs are complete professional artifacts—10-page investment reports, full-stack codebases, multi-visit clinical calculations—rather than short answers or code snippets)

description_authors_words: we introduce MEMLENS, a comprehensive benchmark for memory in multimodal multi-session conversations, comprising 789 questions across five memory abilities (information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge update, and answer refusal) at four standard context lengths (32K-256K tokens)
description_summary: 789 questions requiring genuine visual evidence (not text alone) across five memory abilities, at four context lengths (32K-256K), comparing long-context vision-language models against memory-augmented agents as conversations grow multimodal and long.
external_memory_evidence: “Write-time visual” is the form in which evidence images enter the memory store; “answer-time visual” is the form available to the backbone when the question is asked.
task_format_metric: per-ability accuracy (information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge update, answer refusal)
example_length: 10 turns (turns per session (average)) | 14–93 sessions (sessions per instance (32K-token condition, up to 93 at 256K)) | 1.5 other:images (images per session (average))
length_unit_families: conversational turns; retrieved documents; sessions / episodes
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] MemLens operationalizes long-term/long-context memory difficulty via four standardized input lengths (32K, 64K, 128K, 256K tokens under a cross-modal token-counting scheme), realized by varying the number of haystack sessions from 14 to 93 per instance, rather than via any qualitative duration label
evidence_span: We release four standard context lengths (32K, 64K, 128K, and 256K tokens) under a cross-modal token-counting scheme that aligns text and vision tokens... Sessions/instance 14 → 93

description_authors_words: We exercise the decomposition on a controlled benchmark (LongHorizon-Bench) covering loan qualification and insurance claims adjudication with deterministic ground-truth construction.
description_summary: Loan-qualification and insurance-claims scenarios with deterministic ground truth test long-horizon enterprise agents on four separately scored axes -- factual precision, reasoning coherence, regulatory-compliance reconstruction, calibrated abstention -- under lossy memory.
external_memory_evidence: We test six memory architectures as instruments for exercising the decomposition.
task_format_metric: four-axis alignment scores (factual precision FRP, reasoning coherence RCS, compliance reconstruction CRR, calibrated abstention CAR)
example_length: 6690 tokens (average trajectory length per synthetic case (L)) | 82–95 other:document chunks (document chunks per case trajectory)
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] Long-horizon enterprise agents are systems that run over tens of minutes to hours on a single trajectory, accumulating tens to hundreds of thousands of tokens across tool calls, documents, and intermediate inferences
evidence_span: Long-horizon enterprise agents are systems that run over tens of minutes to hours on a single trajectory, accumulating tens to hundreds of thousands of tokens across tool calls, documents, and intermediate inferences.

description_authors_words: we introduce the Decision-based Implicit Bias (DIB) Benchmark, a large-scale dataset comprising 3,776 decision-making scenarios across nine social domains, designed to quantify implicit bias in long-term decision processes.
description_summary: An LLM agent with long-term memory makes a sequence of 3,776 decisions across nine social domains, testing whether subtle demographic bias accumulates and spreads into unrelated domains as memory grows.
external_memory_evidence: Standard LTM workflows typically follow a storage-retrieval paradigm in which historical interactions are encoded into vector databases or knowledge graphs, and relevant fragments are retrieved to condition future responses
task_format_metric: Generalized Bias Variance (GBV) / Average GBV across social domains, tracked over interaction turns
example_length: 100 turns (length of one simulated long-term-memory interaction lifecycle (per agent-model-memory configuration run)) | 20 turns (interval between periodic bias-audit evaluations (Delta t))
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] long-term memory's continuity is operationalized as a simulated 100-interaction-turn lifecycle (a 'compressed cycle of agent usage'), with periodic bias audits every 20 turns, standing in for the paper's claim that LTM maintains continuity/personalization over 'indefinite interaction lifecycles'
evidence_span: The simulation spans a total of T = 100 interaction turns, designed to simulate a compressed cycle of agent usage.

description_authors_words: We introduce SkillEvolBench, a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating this step from experience reuse to skill formation. It contains 180 tasks across six real-world agent environments, organized into role-conditioned task families with shared latent procedures.
description_summary: 180 tasks across six agent environments where agents must distill episodic trajectories into a reusable external skill library, then get tested on frozen deployment tasks with context shift and adversarial shortcuts.
external_memory_evidence: update an external skill library using compacted trajectories and verifier feedback
task_format_metric: success-rate metrics (RSR/ESR/ARSR/CompSR) comparing skill-based vs. no-skill/raw-trajectory baselines
what_instead_if_absent: the paper frames its object entirely as distilling 'episodic trajectories' into 'reusable procedural skills'; a full-text search found zero occurrences of 'long-horizon' or 'long-term' anywhere in the paper
evidence_span: Large language model (LLM) agents accumulate rich episodic trajectories while solving real-world tasks, but it remains unclear whether such experience can be distilled into reusable procedural skills.

description_authors_words: We introduce LongDS, a benchmark for long-horizon, multi-turn data analysis where agents must maintain, update, restore, and compose evolving analytical states.
description_summary: Tests agentic data analysis over long multi-turn sessions built from real Kaggle notebooks, requiring agents to track, roll back, and recombine an evolving analytical state across an average 11.3-turn dependency span.
external_memory_evidence: the environment is not reset between turns, allowing intermediate code states and results to persist.
task_format_metric: accuracy on state-dependent data-analysis requests across turns
example_length: 32.7 turns (average turns per task (2,225 total turns / 68 tasks)) | 11.3 turns (average dependency span (turns between a state's creation/update and its later dependent reuse))
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] long-horizon agentic data analysis is formulated as analytical state management: covering initial construction, inheritance, updates, counterfactual perturbations, rollbacks, and multi-state composition of an evolving analytical state across turns
evidence_span: We formulate long-horizon agentic data analysis as analytical state management, covering initial construction, inheritance, updates, counterfactual perturbations, rollbacks, and multi-state composition.

description_authors_words: We introduce MobileMem, a benchmark and framework for studying on-device long-term memory, grounded in a year-scale collection of mobile experiences.
description_summary: Year-scale, multimodal mobile-usage trajectories testing an on-device assistant's multi-hop/temporal reasoning, knowledge updating, and implicit preference inference from a user's accumulated app-session experiences rather than isolated facts.
external_memory_evidence: MobileMem is specifically designed to assess the core capabilities of mobile memory architecture, which captures the full lifecycle of user experiences through structured personal knowledge graphs that represent entities, relations, and temporal dynamics across modalities and applications.
task_format_metric: LLM-as-judge accuracy across single/multi-hop, temporal, relationship, and adversarial question types
example_length: 2000000 tokens (length of MobileMem-Omni's synthesized multimodal trajectories (can exceed two million tokens)) | 15–15 other:events (events per temporal event graph (min 2, max 15, per user trajectory))
length_unit_families: stored memory items; tokens / text length
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] long-horizon trajectories are built via a knowledge-grounded synthesis pipeline (KEME) that constructs coherent, temporally consistent user-app session histories 'grounded in a year-scale collection of mobile experiences', explicitly distinguished from collecting isolated facts
evidence_span: We introduce MobileMem, a benchmark and framework for studying on-device long-term memory, grounded in a year-scale collection of mobile experiences. MobileMem employs a knowledge-grounded synthesis pipeline to construct coherent and temporally consistent long-horizon trajectories from user-app sessions.

description_authors_words: We present BenchTrace, a benchmark for evaluating self-evolution ability in LLM agents.
description_summary: Tests whether an agent can diagnose its own past failures from annotated episode snapshots and then avoid repeating that specific failure, via separate reflection-QA and controlled self-evolution simulations.
external_memory_evidence: Self-evolving agents typically improve through non-parametric methods, such as accumulating failure lessons in external memory
task_format_metric: failure-localization / repair metrics (Jaccard-matched failure ranges, FAR, FRC) on annotated failure snapshots
example_length: 6–107 steps (episode length range across the snapshot-reflection dataset (6 to 107 steps))
what_instead_if_absent: the paper uses 'long-horizon agentic tasks' once, as a generic opening descriptor for the field (citing ReAct), and instead precisely defines its own actual constructs: 'episode', 'step', 'trajectory', and 'snapshot' (a stored, static record of an episode)
evidence_span: Large language model (LLM) agents have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across a wide range of complex, long-horizon agentic tasks (Yao et al., 2022).

description_authors_words: we additionally construct ProactiveMemBench, the first benchmark for evaluating proactive memory triggering
description_summary: Tests whether a conversational agent spontaneously initiates memory retrieval from context, rather than only retrieving in response to an explicit query, scored by recall/precision of proactively surfaced memories.
external_memory_evidence: MemCog organizes user knowledge as Navigable Memory Store with associative link graphs
task_format_metric: Recall@5/Precision (LLM+human judged) on proactive memory surfacing; QA accuracy on LoCoMo/LongMemEval
example_length: 20 sessions (sessions per test instance (100 sessions / 5 topic domains = 20 sessions per domain-repeat)) | 400 turns (dialogue turns per topic-domain repeat (2000 turns / 5 domains))
what_instead_if_absent: the paper uses 'long-term memory' and 'extended interaction histories' as an unexamined backdrop for its actual contribution (a navigable, multi-step memory-retrieval architecture, 'Memory-as-Cognition'), never itself stating a threshold or contrast for what counts as long-term
evidence_span: Long-term memory... is fundamental to maintaining coherent, personalized interactions across extended dialogues, enabling agents to capture evolving user knowledge from fragmented conversations and generate historically informed responses beyond fixed context windows.

description_summary: Held-out conversational-turn evaluation (MAPLE-Personas) scoring an LLM-judged personalization-quality metric (trait incorporation rate) for agents built on MAPLE's separate memory/learning/personalization sub-agent architecture, versus a stateless baseline.
external_memory_evidence: The Memory sub-agent uses lightweight filesystem storage with JSON-serialized records organized into three directories: users/ (profile data), episodic/ (session histories), and semantic/ (extracted insights).
task_format_metric: LLM-judge personalization quality (trait incorporation, perfect-score rate) on held-out conversational turns
example_length: 10 turns (turns per synthesized conversational trajectory (8 learning-phase turns + 2 evaluation-phase turns))
what_instead_if_absent: the paper cites prior systems' use of 'long-term memory' (HippoRAG's hippocampal-indexing inspiration, recursive-summarization dialogue memory) but never itself states what makes an interaction long-term/long-horizon for its own 10-turn persona-evaluation design
evidence_span: HippoRAG (Gutierrez et al., 2024) takes inspiration from hippocampal indexing theory of human long-term memory.

description_authors_words: we build an end-to-end benchmark and evaluation framework centered on an LLM-based 1-in-5 selection task, which measures both memory quality and downstream reranking utility.
description_summary: Tests whether distilling a shopper's purchase history into concise preference memory improves an LLM reranker's ability to pick the one correct product from five candidates, versus using raw history or no memory.
external_memory_evidence: ## External memory baselines. We further compare with two memory-centric systems, MR.Rec and Mem0 . To keep the comparison controlled, we run both methods with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and the same metadata-only history window used by MemRerank . MR.Rec first summarizes category-level preferences and then constructs a user profile.
task_format_metric: MRR@10 / MRR@5 on top-100 personalized product reranking
what_instead_if_absent: the paper repeatedly refers to 'long purchase histories' and 'long-term user context' as the motivating problem, and cites cognitive-architecture work on 'long-horizon reasoning', but never itself states a threshold (e.g. minimum number of purchases) defining what counts as a long history for its own benchmark
evidence_span: LLM-based shopping agents increasingly rely on long purchase histories and multi-turn interactions for personalization, yet naively appending raw history to the prompt is often ineffective due to noise, length, and relevance mismatch.

description_authors_words: we introduce DocOps, a deterministically verifiable evaluation framework underpinned by a hierarchical taxonomy that deconstructs document operations inspired by real-world practices into atomic dimensions and escalating workflow complexities
description_summary: Deterministically verified document-manipulation tasks, from atomic operations to escalating multi-step workflows, exposing failure modes like long-term state-tracking collapse and destructive edits to structural metadata in agentic document editing.
external_memory_evidence: treating documents as first-class, stateful computational objects, where each operation is evaluated as a state transition that must reach the requested state while preserving native-format validity and relevant out-of-scope document state across heterogeneous formats.
task_format_metric: deterministic verifier pass rate across a 4-tier (L1-L4) difficulty taxonomy
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] long-horizon(s) is defined by contrast within the paper's own 4-tier taxonomy: L1/L2 are 'short-horizon planning and local dependency modeling' over a single artifact, while L3/L4 'escalate to long-horizons, cross-document workflows' requiring the agent to maintain global consistency across multiple steps and across documents
evidence_span: While L1 and L2 isolate single and multi-dimensional atomic edits, L3 and L4 escalate to long-horizons, cross-document workflows inspired by real-world human interaction scenarios.

description_authors_words: we propose ForgetBench, a benchmark designed to systematically characterize forgetting behavior in LLMs under continual knowledge editing.

evidence_span: While working memory supports transient information manipulation within a single interaction, long-term memory enables durable knowledge retention and gradual forgetting across extended periods.

description_authors_words: we present EvoCodeBench, a benchmark for evaluating self-evolving LLM-driven coding systems across programming languages with direct comparison to human performance.

Its self-evolving coding agent is bounded to at most three reflection/revision iterations within a single problem-solving episode, which is a short, fixed-budget loop rather than a long-running trajectory or persistent cross-session memory; fit with this charter's long-horizon-execution / long-term-memory definitions is a stretch.

description_authors_words: we introduce CirrusBench, a novel evaluation framework distinguished by its foundation in real-world data from authentic cloud service tickets. CirrusBench preserves the intricate multi-turn logical chains and realistic tool dependencies inherent to technical service environments.

description_authors_words: we construct two real-conversation benchmarks (LoCoMo-Contam and MSC-Contam) by planting controlled single-detail corruptions in long-term conversations from LoCoMo and MSC, and complement them with a structured synthetic corpus (MemContam)
description_summary: Real (LoCoMo/MSC-derived) and synthetic conversation benchmarks with planted single-detail factual corruptions, testing whether a memory system's write-time admission gate stops a hallucinated fact from persisting as a false premise across later turns.

evidence_span: Long-horizon LLM agents accumulate facts in an external memory store and reason over them in later steps ( Park et al., 2023; Zhou et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2024; Nakano et al., 2022 ). The architecture works only if the writer is reliable: a fact written once is read back many times, so any error introduced at write time becomes a false premise for every subsequent retrieval.

description_authors_words: We present ClawForge, a generator-backed benchmark framework for executable command-line workflows under state conflict... We instantiate this framework as the ClawForge-Bench (17 scenarios, 6 ability categories).

description_authors_words: We present a modular two-agent simulation framework for evaluating conversational shopping assistant architectures.

description_authors_words: we introduce PlayWorld, a benchmark providing 171 scenarios, each with a specified objective.
description_summary: Agent players pursue 171 long-horizon objectives (e.g., turning around to check scene consistency) inside generative video world models, scoring whether the world model maintains persistent geometry and state as it is revisited.

example_length: 10–60 other:seconds (rollout duration per PlayWorld evaluation case)
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] a long-horizon objective is a high-level, scene-grounded goal (e.g. 'turn around 360 degrees', 'walk into the water') that a player pursues via an adaptively-length action sequence, as opposed to a customized, fixed-length predefined action trajectory whose action count/duration is hand-specified per case and does not transfer fairly across models with different action granularity
evidence_span: In practice, a human user usually evaluates a world model by pursuing a high-level, long-horizon objective rather than by checking whether a predefined action trajectory is followed.

description_authors_words: We introduce Finite-State Machine (FSM) Execution as a minimal, fully interpretable framework for evaluating the procedural reasoning capacity of LLMs. In our setup, the model is given an explicit FSM definition and must execute it step-by-step given input actions, maintaining state consistency over multiple turns.

example_length: 50 turns (turns in an FSM-execution task shown in the reported experiment (e.g., a 2-state/40-action task run to 50 steps)) | 40–40 actions (actions in the action-space configurations tested (e.g., 2-state/40-action, 40-state/2-action))
what_instead_if_absent: uses 'long-horizon' repeatedly as a property that degrades with task depth, but never states a definition or threshold for what counts as long-horizon
evidence_span: This suggests that larger models possess superior capabilities for strict rule-adherence and long-term state maintenance, with Qwen3-235b substantially outperforming all other models in this test.

description_authors_words: In LLM-Wikirace, models must efficiently navigate Wikipedia hyperlinks step by step to reach a target page from a given source, requiring look-ahead planning and the ability to reason about how concepts are connected in the real world.

description_authors_words: We introduce InquiTree, a diagnostic environment that formalizes scientific inquiry as interactive Research Trees: directed acyclic graphs capturing the logical dependencies among hypothesis formulation, study design, result interpretation, and belief updating.
description_summary: Agents traverse paper-derived interactive research trees to conduct scientific inquiry, revealing degraded judgment over long interactions and a performance drop on papers published after the model's training cutoff.

With H=4 and 120 listed subtopics in the released IT-18 subset, this yields a theoretical interaction range of roughly 3×120=360 to 11×120=1320 reasoning-action turns for full traversal, placing the benchmark firmly in the long-horizon regime.

description_authors_words: We introduce User Preference Question Answering (UPQA), a short-answer QA dataset constructed from in-situ user queries with varying levels of difficulty.

description_authors_words: We introduce CEO-Bench, a multi-agent benchmark that evaluates LLMs on CEO-level strategic resource reallocation -- the process of redirecting capital across business units in a multi-round, constraint-rich organizational environment.

description_authors_words: this paper introduces Graph Oblivion and Node Erasure (GONE), a benchmark for evaluating knowledge unlearning over structured knowledge graph (KG) facts in LLMs

description_authors_words: To validate the framework, a benchmark dataset of 30 complex disruption scenarios was curated from a qualitative analysis of over 6,000 real-world user reviews.

Long-term memory allows the agent to retain and recall information across different sessions, enabling continuous learning and personalization. This is usually implemented using external data stores like vector databases.

description_authors_words: we introduce LoHoSearch (Long-Horizon Search Agents), a challenging benchmark comprising 544 human-verified questions across 11 domains.

description_authors_words: We introduce LOOPSBENCH, a long-horizon benchmark for loop engineering in coding agent evaluation. Each task is a dependency DAG over separately testable development units with source-evidenced prerequisite edges.

Solution Scale is at least 1,200 in the source specific scale.

description_authors_words: we introduce RoleMemo, a dataset featuring four reasoning tasks where the factual fragments must be interpreted through the persona to reach the correct answer
description_summary: Tests whether a role-playing agent's memory interprets stored facts through its assigned persona's perspective rather than just recalling them, via four reasoning tasks requiring persona-conditioned inference over factual fragments.

long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] role-playing agents excel in short-term interactions, but long-term conversations overwhelm context windows, motivating external memory frameworks
evidence_span: While role-playing agents excel in short-term interactions, long-term conversations overwhelm context windows, motivating external memory frameworks.

description_authors_words: We present Neuromem, a scalable testbed that benchmarks External Memory Modules under an interleaved insertion-and-retrieval protocol and decomposes its lifecycle into five dimensions including memory data structure, normalization strategy, consolidation policy, query formulation strategy, and context integration mechanism.

external_memory_evidence: We present Neuromem , a scalable testbed that benchmarks External Memory Modules under an interleaved insertion-and-retrieval protocol and decomposes its lifecycle into five dimensions including memory data structure , normalization strategy , consolidation policy , query formulation strategy , and context integration mechanism .
task_format_metric: Mean F1 + read/write latency under a streaming insert-retrieve protocol

evidence_span: the absence of established definitions distinguishing short-term working memory from long-horizon storage prevents the application of hybrid consolidation strategies that could otherwise optimize memory state updates based on retention scope, identifying the formalization of these hierarchical tiers as a critical direction for future architectural research

description_authors_words: we introduce LUCid, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,936 user queries paired with long interaction histories, designed to isolate situational relevance from semantic proximity.

evidence_span: LUCid comprises 1,936 realistic user queries whose correct responses hinge on user-specific attributes ... shared within semantically distant sessions of a lifelong interaction history of up to 500 sessions (620K tokens)

description_authors_words: We introduce a comprehensive continual learning dataset and benchmark (CurLL) grounded in human developmental trajectories from ages 5-10... a skill graph that breaks down broad skills into smaller abilities, concrete goals, and measurable indicators
