example_length: 5 other:developmental-stages (sequential developmental stages (ages 5-10, stages 0-4) composing the continual-learning curriculum)
what_instead_if_absent: uses 'long-term utility and relevance of LMs' once in passing as a motivating consequence of static post-training knowledge, but the paper's own construct is 'continual learning' across 5 developmental stages, never framed via a 'long-horizon' label or threshold
evidence_span: In real world, this information continually expands and updates, and this limitation poses a significant challenge to the long-term utility and relevance of LMs.

description_authors_words: The benchmark comprises 193 manually annotated natural-language QA pairs over ∼100 minutes of egocentric RGB video across 8+ diverse environments.
description_summary: 193 manually annotated QA pairs over ~100 minutes of long, free-walking egocentric video across 8+ indoor/outdoor environments, jointly evaluating frame-level retrieval grounding and answer generation for persistent scene memory.
external_memory_evidence: VL-KnG builds persistent memory through knowledge graphs rather than latent representations, enabling explicit, queryable, and interpretable scene memory that is queried without re-processing the video.
task_format_metric: Retrieval Acc@1/MRR@5 + answer accuracy
example_length: 86–103 other:frames (median sampled frames per WalkieKnowledge trajectory/scene) | 290 other:objects (approximate objects tracked per scene)
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] WalkieKnowledge targets long, free-walking egocentric trajectories (median 86 frames, up to 103 frames per trajectory), explicitly contrasted against OpenEQA's short episodes answerable from a handful of frames (32 frames per episode)
evidence_span: Most OpenEQA questions can be answered from a small set of frames, which favors end-to-end VLMs that directly attend to all images, whereas VL-KnG is designed for long-horizon video with many redundant frames, as in WalkieKnowledge (up to 103 frames per trajectory) and NaVQA (up to 431 frames per trajectory).

description_authors_words: we introduce the Personal Agent Sycophancy Benchmark (PASB), a 1,600-task benchmark that traces whether a conversational claim is accepted, written into durable agent state, and reused in a later neutral query.
description_summary: Tests whether a stateful personal agent commits a sycophantically-accepted user claim into durable memory and then reuses it, unprompted, in a later unrelated conversation, isolating the write-to-memory failure from mere agreement.
external_memory_evidence: The five-turn persist stage runs first; after it terminates, we clear the conversation history, planner scratchpad, temporary tool observations, and runtime cache, then launch a fresh three-turn query session against the same workspace. Since that session receives no persist-stage history, any carry-over must occur through durable state written to the workspace.
task_format_metric: six LLM-judge dimensions (Sycophancy, Leak, Upgrade, Amplification, Persistence, Escalation) scored across persist/query stages
example_length: 5 turns (persist-stage turns per task) | 3 turns (query-stage turns per task)
what_instead_if_absent: The opening sentence uses 'long-term user profiles, episodic memories, and reusable skills' as unexamined background motivation; the paper's actual defined construct is 'persistent sycophancy' (a claim being committed into durable state and reused later), not a definition of what makes a memory horizon 'long'.
evidence_span: Stateful personal agents increasingly maintain long-term user profiles, episodic memories, and reusable skills.

description_authors_words: AhaBench asks a more operational question: when a fixed model receives useful experience, does its later behavior improve under a related evaluation condition where the obvious support has been removed, changed, or delayed?
description_summary: Three-part suite (hidden-state puzzles, generated Project-Euler-style math tasks, a Vending-Bench-style profit simulation) measuring whether an agent's performance improves after prior experience once the obvious support is removed, via an Initial/Post-Experience/Learning-Lift scorecard.
task_format_metric: three-part scorecard (Initial Score, Post-Experience Score, Learning Lift) via rubric-based and validator-based scoring
example_length: 365 days (simulated days per Aha-Vending business run) | 20–20 turns (question-answer turns per Aha-Puzzle episode (cap)) | 56 episodes (Aha-Puzzle episodes per language (direct baseline + 7 curriculum slots × 7 identities))
length_unit_families: conversational turns; sessions / episodes; wall-clock time
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] Operating 'over long horizons' means agents ask follow-up questions, reuse worked examples, handle tool feedback, and adapt to delayed consequences — i.e., behavior later in a run is expected to depend on what happened earlier, rather than resetting per prompt.
evidence_span: Modern language agents are expected to operate over long horizons: they ask follow-up questions, reuse worked examples, handle tool feedback, and adapt to delayed consequences. Most evaluations still reset the agent after a prompt or score only the final state of one trajectory.

description_authors_words: We introduce DMV-Bench, the first interactive benchmark for visual memory in multimodal agents, to study this often-neglected property.
description_summary: Agents shop through chains of sessions in a home-furnishing e-commerce environment where each product image carries a unique incidental visual cue; tests whether the agent recalls that cue later, isolating what it saw from what it deliberately recorded.
external_memory_evidence: the memory architecture under test ingests the page autonomously
task_format_metric: task success rate (TSR) on recall-probe tasks at controlled session-boundary 'reach'
example_length: 5–50 sessions (shopping sessions per chain (J), swept across evaluated configurations)
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] DMV-Bench operationalizes 'long-horizon' visual memory via 'recall reach' — the number of session boundaries separating a product visit from its later recall probe — sweeping this reach to produce a retention curve that is a direct readout of how long a visual cue persists in memory.
evidence_span: An axis of interest here is recall reach: how many session boundaries separate the visit from the probe test. Sweeping this reach produces a retention curve, a direct readout of how long a visual cue persists in a given memory.

description_authors_words: we introduce PersonaTrail, a benchmark for personalized web agents operating in a managed open web environment.
description_summary: Web agents must infer a user's preferences and recall facts from realistic past browsing trajectories to complete underspecified navigation tasks in a managed open-web environment.
external_memory_evidence: We further provide Preference-Aware Contextual Memory ( PACMem ), a framework that decomposes raw browsing histories into two types of structured memory: factual memories that summarize individual sessions and preference memories that distill recurring behavioral patterns.
task_format_metric: Task Success Rate on personalized web-navigation queries (preference inference + episodic grounding)
example_length: 19.76–31.05 sessions (average browsing sessions per user history) | 8.23–19.36 steps (average interaction steps per session)
what_instead_if_absent: The paper uses 'long-term' only as an unexamined descriptor of navigation trajectories and personalization ('long-term navigation trajectories', 'long-term validity', 'long-term personalization') without ever stating a session-count or duration threshold distinguishing long-term from short-term browsing history.
evidence_span: Evaluating web agents involves long-term navigation trajectories where input histories accumulate over successive steps, resulting in prohibitive API inference costs for proprietary models.

description_authors_words: We introduce PolyWorkBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate LLM agents on multilingual, long-horizon workplace workflows. PolyWorkBench features 67 tasks across five core domains: commerce, knowledge work, legal analysis, localization, and manufacturing.
description_summary: 67 enterprise workflow tasks across five domains requiring agents to integrate heterogeneous multilingual inputs over long tool-use trajectories, scored by a structural rubric plus executable and LLM-judge checks.
task_format_metric: Grade (structural scoring rubric) + Pytest executable verification + LLM-as-Judge semantic diagnostics
what_instead_if_absent: The paper formalizes a generic multi-step trajectory abstraction (a workflow W=(T,R,τ,E) with τ=(s1,...,sn)) and asserts that 'long-horizon capability is a property of the coupled system', but never states a minimum step count, duration, or contrast baseline that would pin down what counts as 'long-horizon' versus a shorter task.
evidence_span: Under this formulation, long-horizon capability is a property of the coupled system rather than the foundation model alone.

description_authors_words: We introduce S-EMBER (Streaming Egocentric Memory Benchmark for Episodic Retrieval), a large-scale benchmark comprising 3,141 videos totaling 388 hours of organic activity captured via Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.
description_summary: Tests episodic memory retrieval from continuous first-person video streams (388 hours from smart glasses), requiring causal, on-the-fly recall with precise temporal localization rather than offline whole-video search.
task_format_metric: grounded QA accuracy requiring both correct answer and precise temporal localization
example_length: 7.4–20 other:minutes (video length (average)) | 3–6 tasks (questions per video (average))
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] S-EMBER operationalizes testing of long-term/episodic memory by enforcing a one-minute buffer after any event before a question about it may be authored, and requiring annotators to source questions from each subsequent third of the video, ensuring the benchmark tests sustained comprehension over time rather than immediate recall.
evidence_span: The first stage focuses on eliciting natural, perspective-based questions that challenge long-term memory. To ensure the benchmark tests sustained comprehension rather than immediate recall, we enforce a one-minute initial buffer during which no questions may be authored.

description_authors_words: We present V-DyKnow, a Visual Dynamic Knowledge benchmark for evaluating time-sensitive factual knowledge in VLMs.
description_summary: Time-sensitive visual-question benchmark testing whether vision-language models give outdated answers reflecting stale pretraining snapshots, and whether knowledge-editing or multimodal RAG methods can update facts consistently across text and image modalities.
task_format_metric: correctness/consistency classification (Correct/Outdated/Irrelevant) of VLM responses vs. current Wikidata state
what_instead_if_absent: The paper never uses 'long-term' or 'long-horizon' anywhere in the text; it frames its temporal dimension entirely through 'time-sensitive knowledge' and explicit per-fact 'validity intervals' (e.g., a CEO valid '2011-present', a predecessor valid '1997-2011') rather than a long-term/long-horizon construct.
evidence_span: Attributes in Wikidata are connected to subjects through properties and enriched with qualifiers specifying their validity intervals. For example, the subject Apple is associated with attribute Tim Cook via the property CEO, annotated with the validity interval 2011–present.

description_authors_words: we introduce DRIFTLENS, a ground-truth-free framework that maps each expressed reasoning step to a value category and measures divergence between a question's no-memory trajectory and its trajectory under injected user-attribute memory.
description_summary: Measures whether injecting stored user attributes (age, occupation, etc.) into a personalized LLM's context silently shifts its reasoning path on open-ended questions, even when the final answer looks unchanged.
task_format_metric: ground-truth-free reasoning-trajectory divergence (value-category mapping + edit distance/JS distance) between no-memory and memory-injected trajectories
what_instead_if_absent: The paper explicitly disclaims testing long-horizon interaction: it states its study 'focuses on single-turn open-ended guidance under controlled memory perturbations' and names 'long-horizon interaction' only as a direction for future work, never as something DRIFTLENS itself defines or measures.
evidence_span: DriftLens measures changes in externally expressed reasoning trajectories, not hidden model cognition... Finally, our study focuses on single-turn open-ended guidance under controlled memory perturbations. Extending DriftLens to long-horizon interaction, tool-using agents, and deployed memory systems is an important direction for future work.
scope_flag: Paper explicitly scopes itself to single-turn open-ended guidance under a one-shot injected user-attribute (memory is a static persona attribute injected once, not built up via retention/retrieval across sessions), and explicitly names 'long-horizon interaction' as future work rather than something it tests; this is a reasoning-drift diagnostic rather than a long-term/persistent-memory or long-horizon-execution benchmark as the charter intends.

description_authors_words: We present CorporateBench (CB), a human-validated multi-task Q&A benchmark whose scale approaches the conditions LLMs encounter in corporate communication networks, with evaluation corpora surpassing 230,000 documents
description_summary: Synthetic multi-employee corporate document corpora (up to 230,000+ documents, temporally evolving and logically consistent) test information extraction and knowledge-base querying at realistic enterprise scale.
external_memory_evidence: We construct a large-scale benchmark in which answering typical queries requires integrating evidence across many documents, stressing multi-document retrieval and reasoning over enterprise-scale communication sets whose total size can exceed context windows.
task_format_metric: macro-F1 for entity/relationship extraction (incl. temporal accuracy) + topic-level F1 for knowledge-base querying
example_length: 354–232693 other:documents (documents in the evaluation corpus per company-scale variant (S/M/L/XL))
what_instead_if_absent: The paper's sole use of 'long-term' occurs inside a fictional company's flavor-text description ('focusing on long-term value creation') rather than as a definitional framing for the benchmark; 'long-horizon' never occurs. CorporateBench instead frames its temporal dimension via a 'temporally evolving knowledge base' and corpus scale (12 to 10,210 employees; up to 230,000+ documents).
evidence_span: Pound Financial is a mid-market investment firm... The firm maintains a conservative, relationship-driven approach, focusing on long-term value creation rather than quick exits.

aliases: Adaptive Friend Agent; AFA; Persona Attribution Accuracy; PAA
description_authors_words: we construct PAT (Personalized Agent chaT), a synthetic dataset of 58,289 persona-grounded dialogue turns spanning 133 user profiles and 12 real-world scenarios.
description_summary: 58,289 persona-grounded dialogue turns across 133 profiles, used with an interleaved multi-user evaluation protocol and a Persona Attribution Accuracy metric to test whether a shared assistant keeps different users' histories from leaking into each other's responses.
external_memory_evidence: We present the Adaptive Friend Agent (AFA), a modular framework that combines voice-based speaker identification with per-user memory stores to enable identit
task_format_metric: response-quality benchmark + Persona Attribution Accuracy (PAA) in an interleaved multi-user evaluation protocol
example_length: 40 turns (contextually-linked persona-driven questions per persona-scenario (each successive query builds upon the previous one)) | 481.71 words (average prompt length per example (words)) | 76.41 words (average completion length per example (words))
what_instead_if_absent: The paper uses 'long-term memory' as an unexamined given throughout, motivated by contrast with prior single-pair multi-session work (MSC/Beyond Goldfish Memory), but never itself restates or extends that definition with a threshold specific to PAT; PAT's own construction detail is instead a fixed count of 40 contextually-linked questions per persona-scenario, never labeled 'long-term'.
evidence_span: These inconsistencies underscore the need for explicit long-term memory and user modeling. Prior work on personalized dialogue, such as PersonaChat (Zhang et al., 2018) or multi-session chat (Xu et al., 2022), typically focuses on single-user personalization or fixed persona profiles, creating a gap in handling dynamic multi-user settings.

description_authors_words: We introduce two full-text scientific-memory benchmarks, Public AI Memory (PAIM; 81 papers, 66 questions) and Public Transformers (PTr; 252 papers, 98 questions).
description_summary: Tests memory/retrieval systems on restoring specific evidence from full scientific papers (not chat summaries) under an explicit, controlled retrieval-budget protocol, comparing systems fairly rather than via a leaderboard.
external_memory_evidence: LLM agents increasingly rely on long-term memory mechanisms: vector stores, knowledge graphs, episodic logs, extracted facts, and hybrid retrieval pipelines.
task_format_metric: LLM-as-judge rubric score (1-10 scale) across difficulty tiers under a budgeted context-restoration protocol
example_length: 2150000 tokens (total persistent-store corpus size (tokens) that must be searched to answer one question, Paim benchmark) | 2170000 tokens (total corpus size (tokens), size-matched PTr subset)
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] the paper reframes 'long-term memory' evaluation for research agents as 'context restoration': not passive store-and-recall of a single fact from conversations, but reconstructing an interconnected body of literature evidence at the right granularity and within a budget, in contrast to the standard conversational recall framing (LongMemEval, LoCoMo, BEAM) which it says 'does not transfer cleanly' to this setting.
evidence_span: In our opinion, the standard conversational framing does not transfer cleanly to research agents... We call this task context restoration: the memory must return enough grounded evidence for a downstream model to compose a faithful answer.

description_authors_words: a seeded life-script sampler emits facts with validity intervals, volatility classes, and source channels before any text exists; an LLM renderer writes chat and email from per-event fact manifests; a fidelity verifier confirms every planted fact
description_summary: Synthetic chat/email corpus (~380 questions) built script-first so gold answers are correct by construction, testing memory systems at two horizons (three vs. nine weeks) and finding backend rankings invert as history grows longer.
external_memory_evidence: On this instrument we benchmark five memory architectures against a no-memory control under a fixed answerer, a versioned LLM judge treated as part of the benchmark, and threefold stochastic replication, across two history horizons.
task_format_metric: versioned LLM-judge QA accuracy across two horizons (three vs. nine weeks of history)
example_length: 3 other:weeks (accumulated user history at the short horizon) | 9 other:weeks (accumulated user history at the long horizon)
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] the paper operationalizes two horizons for its longitudinal evaluation: a 'short horizon' at three weeks of accumulated history and a 'long horizon' at nine weeks, and shows that backend rankings invert between the two.
evidence_span: we find backend rankings invert with history length: the budgeted curated-map memory that leads at three weeks of history loses recall of evicted content by nine weeks (96% to 72%), while a provenance-typed graph rises to 90% - short-horizon benchmarks can mis-rank the very systems a long-lived assistant needs.

description_authors_words: we introduce Claw-Anything, a benchmark that expands agent context along three dimensions: long-horizon activity histories, interdependent backend services, and integrated GUI and CLI interaction across multiple devices.
description_summary: Simulated months of a user's multi-device digital activity, with conflicting signals and irrelevant noise injected over time, test whether an always-on personal assistant reasons over the full accumulated context and proactively anticipates needs.
external_memory_evidence: We also modify the agent’s tool interface so that, at evaluation time, the agent can access the app databases populated during task generation.
task_format_metric: task success rate (pass@1)
example_length: 3 months (span of the long-horizon activity/event stream per task environment)
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] the environment's own formal definition includes a component L, 'a long-horizon activity stream covering over three months of system-level and service-specific logs' - i.e. long-horizon is operationalized as an activity history spanning more than three months.
evidence_span: Formally, each environment is defined as E = (P, D, F, L)... and L denotes a long-horizon activity stream covering over three months of system-level and service-specific logs.

description_authors_words: We introduce PersonaMem-v3, a real-world-grounded benchmark and evaluation harness for omni-platform personal intelligence.
description_summary: Built from over a million real anonymized engagement histories, tests whether an agent builds cross-platform (social media, chat, calendar) user understanding to personalize, recommend, and act proactively without over-personalizing, as user preferences evolve.
external_memory_evidence: Each platform is saved as its own database file, including Instagram, Facebook, Threads, Chatbot, Meta AI Studio, and Calendar.
task_format_metric: task accuracy / NDCG@5 (recommendation reranking) / restraint accuracy across multiple personalization task families
example_length: 4000 other:events (engagement events per user history (average)) | 30 days (observation window per user history)
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] long-term preferences require a cross-reference (repeated-evidence) score of at least 20 (explicit evidence) or 50 (implicit evidence) to enter the user profile, versus a lower threshold of 3 for short-term intents, reflecting that long-term preferences must be corroborated by many more independent events than short-term intents.
evidence_span: For long-term preferences, the cross-reference threshold is 20 when the evidence is explicit and 50 when it is implicit. Short-term intents use a lower threshold of 3 because they naturally have less time to accumulate repeated evidence.

description_authors_words: MedLoCoMo is a Medical Long-Context Memory benchmark for patient-specific clinical reasoning over multi-admission medical dialogue... generating evidence linked QA items over single-admission, cross-admission, and adversarial unanswerable settings.
description_summary: 100 synthetic patient timelines (avg. ~1,670 turns) built from MIMIC-IV records, testing whether models answer, connect across admissions, or correctly abstain on unanswerable questions about a patient's longitudinal history.
task_format_metric: token-F1 + LLM-judge accuracy + abstention accuracy (composite Score)
example_length: 1669.8 turns (turns per patient conversation (average)) | 29.7 sessions (sessions (admissions) per patient conversation (average)) | 74512.2 tokens (tokens per patient conversation (average))
length_unit_families: conversational turns; sessions / episodes; tokens / text length
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] long-context/longitudinal reasoning is defined by contrast with 'short-context knowledge or single-document grounding': it requires using, connecting, and abstaining over patient histories that span multiple hospital admissions (sessions), unlike single-document EHR QA.
evidence_span: Existing medical QA benchmarks largely test short-context knowledge or single-document grounding, leaving open whether LLMs can use, connect, and abstain over longitudinal patient histories.

description_authors_words: we introduce EmbodiedWorldBench, an executable benchmark with 16 indoor, outdoor, and hybrid scenes, four difficulty levels, and over 200 tasks involving navigation, object search, NPC dialogue, dynamic events, and trace-grounded scoring
description_summary: Tests a robotic agent OS on 200+ embodied tasks (navigation, object search, NPC dialogue, dynamic events) across 16 scenes and four difficulty levels, using multi-modal graph memory and trace-grounded scoring.
external_memory_evidence:
## 5.2 Memory Evaluation

 This section evaluates the proposed memory module independently from the agent-control component.
task_format_metric: task success + goal completion (trace-grounded scoring)
what_instead_if_absent: the paper uses 'long-horizon' extremely pervasively (embodied tasks, planning, execution, reasoning) as an unexamined qualifier throughout, but never states a step-count, scene-count, or duration threshold defining what makes a task long-horizon; the only quantification given is task/scene counts for the benchmark as a whole (16 scenes, 200+ tasks, 4 difficulty levels), not a per-task horizon length.
evidence_span: Recent VLM and VLA systems have improved robotic perception and action prediction, yet long-horizon embodied agents still require a general runtime layer for reasoning, memory, tool use, verification, and cross-embodiment execution.

description_authors_words: we present MobilePA-Bench, an interactive, stateful, and tool-centric benchmark for evaluating the tool-calling and planning abilities of mobile planning agents.
description_summary: Stateful mobile-OS sandbox with 212 tools across 13 domains testing a planning agent's tool use, sub-agent delegation, and use of stored memories/user profiles to resolve implicit instructions, scored by gated per-dimension success rate.
external_memory_evidence: Search and retrieval interfaces (e.g., search_user_memory ) over persistent user-profile and contextual databases.
task_format_metric: gated success rate per capability dimension (Basic Tool Use, Sub-agent Collaboration, Memory Usage, Skill Usage)
example_length: 15–15 steps (maximum step budget per task trajectory (T_max, hard cap))
what_instead_if_absent: uses 'long-horizon' and 'long-term user context/habits' repeatedly as unexamined descriptors of tasks and memory retrieval, without ever stating a threshold or scale that makes something long-horizon
evidence_span: an agent must dynamically retrieve long-term user context (Memory Retrieval), invoke structured backend APIs for batch operations (Skills Execution)...

description_authors_words: we establish OS-Marathon, comprising 100 vast-horizon, repetitive tasks across 5 scenarios and 10 domains, on which our evaluation reveals that leading state-of-the-art (SOTA) CUAs struggle substantially.
description_summary: Computer-use agents perform vast-horizon repetitive workflows, such as processing many receipts, whose length scales with data volume, testing whether they learn and reuse recurring sub-workflow structure across instances.
external_memory_evidence: Each node in the graph represents one demonstrated step and stores two density levels, a textual description for compact retrieval and the screenshots for detailed visual context, while directed edges carry the executed action information.
task_format_metric: field-level / subtask-level success rate on repetitive computer-use workflows
example_length: 50–200 steps (execution steps per task, end-to-end (OS-Marathon)) | 30 steps (execution steps per subtask (matches typical OSWorld/OdysseyBench full-task horizon)) | 9000000 tokens (multimodal tokens for a demonstration covering a single subtask (~30 steps))
length_unit_families: agent steps / actions; tokens / text length
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] the paper distinguishes three task categories by required steps: 'Atomic tasks are self-contained and require no long context. Long-horizon tasks chain atomic tasks into non-repetitive workflows... Vast-horizon, repetitive tasks scale with the number of data instances'; existing long-horizon benchmarks (OSWorld, OdysseyBench) typically require ~30 steps, whereas OS-Marathon's vast-horizon tasks span roughly 50 to 200 steps end-to-end
evidence_span: Figure 2: Task comparison. Atomic tasks are self-contained and require no long context. Long-horizon tasks chain atomic tasks into non-repetitive workflows whose instructions enumerate them explicitly. Vast-horizon, repetitive tasks scale with the number of data instances and are specified by high-level instructions that the agent must decompose itself.

description_authors_words: We introduce EgoMonth, the first month-level egocentric video understanding benchmark... comprises over 300 hours of first-person daily-life recordings from 20 participants spanning 20 to 120 days, paired with 1,443 human-crafted multiple-choice question-answer pairs
description_summary: Multiple-choice QA over 20-120 days of continuous first-person video per participant, using a 14-task hierarchy (schema consolidation, episodic indexing, cascading reasoning) to test spatiotemporal memory across real elapsed days, not just long context length.
task_format_metric: 14-task multiple-choice QA accuracy, macro-averaged across three cognitive levels
example_length: 20–120 days (days spanned by a single participant's continuous recording) | 15 hours (video hours per participant (derived: 300+ total hours / 20 participants))
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] the paper defines month-level 'long-term spatiotemporal memory' by recording span: participants are recorded continuously for 20 to 120 days (vs. the prior state-of-the-art EgoLife's one week), such that decisive events can be 'separated by days or weeks' and models must retain evidence 'across extended experience'
evidence_span: EgoMonth extends the span from one week to 20–120 days, covers independent daily routines across diverse participants and environments, and emphasizes sparse event retrieval, long-term behavioral consolidation, and cross-day spatiotemporal reasoning.

description_authors_words: a sequence of $196$ dependent tool calls over $64$ rounds while it carries four $32$-bit words $(a,b,c,d)$ in its own context from one call to the next.
description_summary: Testbed requiring an LLM to execute MD5 hashing step-by-step across 196 dependent tool calls, isolating pure long-horizon state-tracking (exact intermediate-value carry-over) from instruction-following, checked bit-exact against a ground-truth trace.
task_format_metric: exact-match digest correctness after N dependent tool calls (state-carrying success)
example_length: 196 actions (dependent tool calls per MD5 execution run) | 64 other:rounds (MD5 compression rounds carried across the 196 tool calls per run)
long_horizon_definition: [contrastive] the paper contrasts its 196-dependent-tool-call test against the field's usual degradation point, noting that 'quality degrades as the context grows past a few tens of thousands of tokens or a few tens of turns', and explicitly designs its test to sustain exact state across a much longer, strictly dependent sequence to isolate long-horizon state-tracking from instruction interpretation
evidence_span: quality degrades as the context grows past a few tens of thousands of tokens or a few tens of turns (Liu et al. 2024; Modarressi et al. 2025).

aliases: Memory Evaluation for Realistic Instrumented Tasks
description_authors_words: We present MERIT (Memory Evaluation for Realistic Instrumented Tasks), a benchmark and harness that measures the marginal utility of memory for task-executing agents under explicit cost accounting.
description_summary: Measures whether remembering an earlier episode's facts actually changes what a tool-using agent does on a later dependent task, with an automated leak check, an updated-fact difficulty ladder, and full dollar-cost metering.
external_memory_evidence:
MERIT provides episodic tool-use tasks in three
domains whose dependence on earlier-episode facts is verified by an
automated leak check
task_format_metric: task success rate on dependent-task episodes, under a difficulty ladder, with full token/dollar cost metering
long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] long-term memory is defined as 'information persisted across sessions and selectively recalled', for agents that 'plan, call tools, and act over multiple sessions'
evidence_span: A central architectural question for every such deployment is whether and how to give the agent long-term memory: information persisted across sessions and selectively recalled.

description_authors_words: We introduce Multi-Horizon Task Environments (MHTEs): a distinct problem class requiring coherent execution across dozens of interleaved tasks (45+, 500-1500+ steps) within persistent execution contexts spanning hours
description_summary: Corporate-environment simulation with 45+ concurrent long-horizon tasks (500-1500+ steps) and dependencies, testing computer-use agents' resistance to context saturation, memory interference, and reprioritization overhead as task load scales.
external_memory_evidence: CorpGen implements a tiered memory system with three layers: Working Memory (Intra-Cycle) , which holds active task state and immediate reasoning and resets each cycle; Structured Long-Term Memory , which stores typed artifacts such as plans, action summaries, and reflections; and Semantic Memory , which supports similarity-based retrieval over unstructured past context using Mem0
task_format_metric: task completion rate under scaling concurrent task load (25%-100%)
example_length: 45 tasks (concurrent interleaved tasks per persistent execution context (minimum)) | 500–1500 steps (total steps across all interleaved tasks per execution context) | 10–30 steps (steps per individual task within an MHTE)
long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] Multi-Horizon Task Environments (MHTEs) are defined as requiring 'coherent execution across dozens of interleaved tasks (45+, 500-1500+ steps) within persistent execution contexts spanning hours', each individual task itself requiring its own long-horizon plan of 10-30+ steps, contrasted against single-task long-horizon benchmarks like ALFWorld/WebArena that require only 10-20 steps for one task
evidence_span: We introduce Multi-Horizon Task Environments (MHTEs): a distinct problem class requiring coherent execution across dozens of interleaved tasks (45+, 500–1500+ steps) within persistent execution contexts spanning hours.

description_authors_words: we introduce SubtleMemory, a benchmark for fine-grained relational memory discrimination in long-running AI agents.
description_summary: 1,522 evaluation instances built from relation-controlled memory variants (complementary, nuanced, contradictory) embedded in realistic agent histories test whether an agent recovers correct relational structure among related memories, not just isolated recall.
external_memory_evidence: We evaluate three deployment settings. (1) Six standalone memory systems: Mem0, MemOS, EverMemOS, MIRIX, A-Mem, and MemoBase  ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2026a ; Wang and Chen, 2025 ; Xu et al., 2025 ; MemoBase, 2026 ) . (2) Two Claw-style agents with native memory mechanisms: OpenClaw and MetaClaw  ( OpenClaw, 2026 ; Xia et al., 2026 ) . (3) OpenClaw augmented with three plugin-based memory modules: Mem0, MemOS, and EverMemOS.
task_format_metric: answer correctness rate on queries requiring discrimination among semantically related memory items (complementary/nuanced/contradictory relation types)
example_length: 236.4 sessions (memory-bearing sessions per user history (average)) | 211600 tokens (session tokens per user history (average))
what_instead_if_absent: repeatedly uses 'long-term'/'long-horizon' to describe accumulated persistent-assistant interactions (drawing an analogy to human memory-interference research) without ever stating a numeric or contrastive threshold for what counts as long; the closest thing is the benchmark's own construction statistics (sessions/tokens per history), which are dataset-construction facts rather than a stated definition

description_authors_words: We introduce EnterpriseMem-Bench, a multi-turn Text-to-SQL benchmark of 300 sessions and 1,400 turns built programmatically from three enterprise domains (BIRD financial, SEC EDGAR, Northwind), with deterministic ground truth and per-turn memory-critical annotation.

Each session therefore starts with a fresh working memory regardless of condition. Episodic memory is implemented as a ChromaDB 1.0.9 collection using the in-built ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding model.

evidence_span: Multi-turn Text-to-SQL—where analysts refine structured database queries across conversational turns—is central to enterprise AI deployments, yet Text-to-SQL systems remain predominantly evaluated in single-turn settings.

description_authors_words: We introduce StreamMemBench, a streaming benchmark that constructs a two-step task sequence around each evidence anchor from EgoLife egocentric streams. We construct Agent Personalized Benchmark (APeB) from action logs, pairing underspecified intents with rich histories and user-viewed candidate items.

description_authors_words: We introduce LOCOMO-CONV, a conversational memory benchmark derived from LoCoMo with four query styles: dialog, implicit, counterfactual, and composed.

Across five representative memory systems, we evaluate both retrieval recall and
end-to-end response quality.

description_authors_words: we introduce MemEvoBench, the first benchmark evaluating long-horizon memory safety in LLM agents against adversarial memory injection, noisy tool outputs, and biased feedback

They argue that within the closed loop of continuous interaction and self-updates, cumulative biases cause agents to deviate from their initial objectives... This phenomenon refers to the gradual behavioral drift resulting from repeated exposure to misleading information.

description_authors_words: we introduce CAPA, which characterizes personalized coding ambiguity through six mechanisms and injects these mechanisms into unambiguous executable tasks using a controlled three-stage generation pipeline.
description_summary: 600 coding sessions across 60 user-ambiguity cells test whether a coding assistant reuses a user's prior resolved sessions to recognize recurring personalized ambiguity and produce correct code with fewer clarification requests.

The existing methods retrieve, summarize, or organize evidence from resolved same-user sessions instead of directly inserting the complete raw history.

evidence_span: A long-term coding assistant should similarly infer such recurring interpretations from prior coding sessions; otherwise, it must repeatedly request clarification or continue making the same incorrect assumption, increasing interaction and user cognitive load.

description_authors_words: FM-Bench (Football Management Benchmark) measures this. An LLM agent runs a football club for 20 in-game years through 26 tools and roughly 340 to 400 decision stops.
description_summary: An LLM agent manages a football club for 20 simulated years, making budgeted transfer, contract, and lineup decisions, scored by a deterministic cumulative outcome with no LLM judge, alone or head-to-head against rivals.

long_horizon_definition: [explicit-stated] This combination is what we call management: running an organization against rivals pursuing the same opportunities, over a horizon so long that early decisions reshape the world, with performance judged cumulatively under the conditions those decisions created. ... Cumulative consequences: the best actions pay off years later, losing positions compound yet remain recoverable.
evidence_span: This combination is what we call management, running an organization against rivals pursuing the same opportunities, over a horizon so long that early decisions reshape the world, with performance judged cumulatively under the conditions those decisions created.

description_authors_words: we introduce a new benchmark designed to evaluate how knowledge editing methods handle the logical consequences of a single fact edit. Our benchmark extracts relevant logical rules from a knowledge graph for a given edit. Then, it generates multi-hop questions based on these rules to assess the impact on logical consequences.

what_instead_if_absent: the paper never uses 'long-horizon'/'long-term'; it frames its contribution entirely as evaluating the LOGICAL CONSEQUENCES of a single fact edit (multi-hop entailment via mined logical rules), a knowledge-editing-consistency question rather than a duration- or session-based construct.
evidence_span: we introduce a new benchmark designed to evaluate how knowledge editing methods handle the logical consequences of a single fact edit. Our benchmark extracts relevant logical rules from a knowledge graph for a given edit.

description_authors_words: we establish PATH-Bench, a benchmark for path-dependent evaluation of lifelong agents
description_summary: Tests how the specific order of an agent's accumulated experience (helpful vs. interfering) shapes forward transfer, backward transfer, and forgetting, across single-turn code generation and multi-turn tool-use tasks.

evidence_span: Performance is path-dependent when P_q(H) varies with the content and order of H.

description_authors_words: We introduce SCALE-QA, a constraint-grounded task QA benchmark for flat unsegmented threads targeting episode integrity failure. The dataset contains 3,000 audited questions across 10 domains, uses deterministic four-way multiple-choice grading, and includes a deterministic runtime builder.
description_summary: 3,000 four-way multiple-choice questions embedded in single, unsegmented long chat threads (up to 1M tokens) where the correct answer depends on identifying which earlier turn in the flat thread is the causally relevant episode.
task_format_metric: deterministic four-way MCQ accuracy + CL Hit (closed-loop evidence hit)

evidence_span: Unlike chunks, which are mechanically defined retrieval units, or sessions, which are explicit temporal interaction units, operative episodes are latent semantic-decision units whose boundaries must be inferred.

description_authors_words: we construct a large-scale benchmark, Multi-Rank Lifelong Free-text Editing Benchmark (MRLF-Bench), containing 16,835 free-text edit requests.

LLMs perform dynamic updates through continual knowledge editing, where each update builds upon the model state obtained from the preceding edit.
evidence_span: We propose the Lifelong Free-text Knowledge Editing (LF-Edit) task, which enables LLMs to continuously learn knowledge from free-text inputs, and preserves previous knowledge at the same time... The LF-Edit task requires LLMs to continuously receive a free-text stream of edit instances S={S1,S2,...,Sn}

description_authors_words: We present a diagnostic methodology that instruments security tasks with checkpoints, separates failures before and after capability exposure, and uses controlled interventions to test suspected upstream bottlenecks.

description_authors_words: we propose MultiMedEdit, the first benchmark tailored to evaluating KE in clinical multimodal tasks. Our framework spans both understanding and reasoning task types, defines a three-dimensional metric suite (reliability, generality, and locality).

This setup is used to examine the model's ability to retain newly added knowledge, mitigate cumulative interference, and robustly resist catastrophic forgetting during long-term editing.

This setup is used to examine the model's ability to retain newly added knowledge, mitigate cumulative interference, and robustly resist catastrophic forgetting during long-term editing.

description_authors_words: We introduce RNG-Bench (Reconstructive Non-Markov Games), a benchmark suite designed to isolate a base model's ability to reconstruct past observations and act on them during multi-step interaction
description_summary: Two controllable games (Matching Pairs card recall, 3D Maze spatial integration) isolating pure hidden-observation memory from decision-making, using a head-to-head duel protocol and a Memory Gap metric against an oracle-state condition.

evidence_span: In long-horizon interaction, the correct action often depends on observations from several turns earlier rather than on the current view. A single recall error can change subsequent observations and compound throughout the episode. We refer to this regime as Non-Markov.

description_authors_words: we instantiate it in StateMemBench, a benchmark of 234 multi-session scenarios spanning two conversation-length regimes.

example_length: 165 turns (median turns per scenario (Set A, short)) | 18 sessions (sessions per scenario (Set A, short)) | 599 turns (median turns per scenario (Set B, long))

description_authors_words: We introduce FinPerMA, an event-grounded benchmark that evaluates personalized memory against frozen longitudinal investor trajectories.

description_authors_words: MemArena fills these gaps with a single-world conversational benchmark built with its MASim agent simulator, for 50 agents over 15 days (10.3M dialog-text tokens, 24.1K text-only ego-observed tokens/agent/day). description_authors_words: we introduce UtilMem, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 1,717 instances across five domains, designed to evaluate four underexplored aspects of memory utilization: reasoning over dense histories, identifying implicitly relevant memories, synthesizing distributed evidence into summaries, analyses, or plans...
description_summary: Tests whether a memory system can integrate distributed, implicit, and noisy evidence across a conversation history into coherent outputs, not just retrieve isolated facts, while resisting semantically similar distractors.

long_horizon_definition: [operational-threshold] UtilMem's per-sample haystack is built to a mean 120K-token budget (deliberately matched to LongMemEval-S's 122K) but with 3-7 ground-truth evidence sessions per sample (vs. a median of 2 in LongMemEval-S) and a total of roughly 60-70 sessions per sample once strong/weak distractors are added — i.e., 'long-term' is operationalized via evidence multiplicity and distractor density at a fixed token scale, not merely raw length.

description_authors_words: We introduce OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on long-horizon office-suite tasks with task-level economic grounding... description_authors_words: we propose DunphyBench, a new benchmark for evaluating agents on long-horizon human-centered embodied decision-making, where the agent must navigate through multiple embodied housing environments and make decisions that align with multi-dimensional human preferences.

description_authors_words: We propose MANBENCH, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate agent behaviors across four common task types that are susceptible to the Mandela effect, using five interaction protocols that vary in agent roles and memory timescales.

description_authors_words: we introduce H2HMem, a Human-to-Human Multimodal Memory Benchmark for evaluating memory capabilities in complex human-human interactions.

evidence_span: During long-term interactions, raw memory entries extracted by the system are often fragmented and lack logical consolidation.

description_authors_words: we introduce RoboGraph, a robotic task compiler that translates state-transition dependencies into executable symbolic graphs... we release a benchmark comprising 588 episodes across 84 scenes with varying TSHs.

description_authors_words: we construct LitCharToM, a benchmark of character-centric questions across four ToM dimensions from classic literature.

evidence_span: LitCharToM provides rich scenarios with complex social dynamics and long-term narrative dependencies, enabling comprehensive assessment of contextual understanding.

description_authors_words: We introduce Mr.LHDR (Multimodal real-world Long-Horizon Deep Research), a benchmark for evaluating real-world deep research over long, irreducible chains of interdependent evidence across eight categories... requires an average of 12.1 necessary intermediate conclusions with a mean dependency depth of 10.4 before reaching a short, unique, and verifiable answer.
